meta.note: Rule rows (PWC25 shape): id, world, statement (paraphrased), locators, speaker, mechanism, seam (AB code), derives (blocked slugs a playable model exists for), default_dial_reason, licence. Proposals: a batched reader (gpt-6-luna) read the books in shards of about 8,000 words; nothing here was human-checked, and no source text is kept.

rules.statement: Most curses do not end through repeated successful saves; they generally require magic or a particular remedy. A curse may stay constant or worsen over time, and dispel magic never ends a curse spell.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Curses (pf1-rules#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistent effects that need a specific cure; a world can make removal easier or harder, with lasting afflictions as the cost.

rules.statement: A spontaneous curse can be attempted only under exceptional stress and no more than once per month. The curser needs at least 5 ranks in Knowledge (arcana) or Knowledge (religion), and can choose a curse whose DC is no higher than 10 plus those ranks; doing so reduces Charisma by 2 for as long as the curse lasts, and the curser cannot dismiss it.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Types of Curses (pf1-rules#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rare, crisis-driven cursing with a Charisma loss; a world can relax the stress or frequency limits, at the cost of making curses more common.

rules.statement: Removing a curse can require extra magic or specific actions. A curse can increase the removal DC by 2, 5, or 10, resist remove curse and break enchantment entirely, or require limited wish, miracle, or wish; making amends may allow a new save, with forgiveness from the curse-layer granting +4.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Breaking the Curse; Alternative Means of Relief (pf1-rules#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to remedies tied to the curse’s cause; a world can allow spell-only removal, trading narrative obligations for easier relief.

rules.statement: A curse that spreads by a chosen route can expose creatures trying to magically cure its original victim: they must save or contract it themselves. The afflicted creature’s own magical attempts to remove it automatically fail, though others can still try.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Curse Templates — Contagious Curse (pf1-rules#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a transmission route and risky treatment; a world can make the curse noncontagious or permit self-cure, reducing spread or treatment danger.

rules.statement: A death curse uses a save DC of 10 + half the curser’s Hit Dice + its Charisma modifier. When the curser is first restored to life, the victim gets another save to end the curse; helping with the resurrection grants +4 on that save.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Curse Templates — Death Curse (pf1-rules#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a curse linked to the curser’s death and return; a world can omit the extra save, making revival less likely to relieve the victim.

rules.statement: A generational curse also affects the target’s descendants, potentially only particular children. Curing one individual does not prevent the curse from afflicting later generations; it usually ends only through special means or extinction of the family line.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Curse Templates — Generational Curse (pf1-rules#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to inheritance that survives individual cures; a world can restrict inheritance to a chosen lineage or make each generation independently curable.

rules.statement: A regional curse has an area and a removal DC, and its effects may allow no save. To remove one with remove curse, the caster usually treats the land as an object and must be at the emanation’s center or another place closely linked to the curse.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Cursed Land (pf1-rules#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an area-wide effect with a focal point for removal; a world can make it removable from anywhere, reducing the need to explore the cursed region.

rules.statement: A tomb curse specifies triggering actions, a save, a primary effect on a failed save, and a secondary effect that applies to everyone who triggers it regardless of the save. The secondary effect stacks with the primary effect and is usually limited to the tomb; most are removed by remove curse, but stronger ones can require greater magic or specific acts.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Tomb Curses — Elements of a Tomb Curse (pf1-rules#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to trigger-based curses with an unavoidable local consequence; a world can make secondary effects save-negated, weakening the price of trespass.

rules.statement: A location curse triggers at initiative 10 in a surprise round; nearby characters may try to notice it at the start of that round. Invisibility may fool one, but hide from undead does not, and its effects are not normally mind-affecting or fear effects.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Location-Based Curse Rules — Combat; Descriptors (pf1-rules#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to curses manifesting at initiative 10 and not counting as mental or fear effects; a setting can make them more like haunts, at the cost of changing how protections and detection interact.

rules.statement: Unless a curse specifies otherwise, curses of CR 5 or less can be permanently removed at their location with remove curse, CR 10 or less with break enchantment, CR 15 or less with limited wish, and CR 20 or less with miracle or wish. Removing one ends ongoing victim effects; spells used directly on a victim follow the same CR limits, while a curse with a release entry may require a separate action that frees one or all victims as specified.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Location-Based Curse Rules — Destruction; Effect and Release (pf1-rules#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to tiered removal magic cast at the cursed place; a world can require a costly release act or restrict which victims it frees, with sacrifice or access to rare means as the price.

rules.statement: Detect undead cannot find location curses, but detect magic can reveal their area borders. Spellcraft at DC 10 + curse CR identifies malice; each 5 points by which the check exceeds that DC reveals one of trigger, effect, or release. Dispel magic damages a curse for 1d6 per two caster levels, and reducing it to 0 hit points only suppresses it until it resets.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Location-Based Curse Rules — Detection; Neutralization; Weaknesses (pf1-rules#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to magical detection and temporary suppression rather than destruction; a setting can make vulnerabilities more discoverable or permanent, trading mystery for reliable counterplay.

rules.statement: Location-curse construction adjustments are +1–2 CR for unique destruction requirements, +2 for effects that persist after manifestation stops, and –1 if the curse has multiple or broadly accessible damage methods. Trigger modifiers include –1 for touching a specific object or targeting a limited group; release modifiers are –2 for an action anyone can perform with local materials and +1 for a costly sacrifice or difficult-to-find requirements.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Creating Location-Based Curses (pf1-rules#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to adjusting challenge rating for persistence, trigger selectivity, and release burden; a world can turn those dials to make curses more selective or harder to lift, with increased danger reflected in CR.

rules.statement: A disease template can be applied to any disease, and several templates can stack. Identifying a templated strain as different from its common variant requires at least 1 hour examining it and its victims, then a Heal check at DC equal to the disease save DC + 10.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Diseases — Disease Templates (pf1-rules#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing multiple templates and requiring trained examination to detect them; a world can make mutations subtler or easier to diagnose, trading preparedness against uncertainty.

rules.statement: Drug use immediately grants the listed effect and ability damage, and requires a Fortitude save against addiction. Taking another dose while ability damage from a prior dose remains raises that drug’s addiction DC by 2 each time; addiction penalties are suppressed while the user benefits from that drug, then return when its effects expire. A character can try to overcome addiction only after a day without the drug, and using it again resets the DC to its highest value and erases accumulated successful recovery saves.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Drugs — Drugs; Addiction; Curing Addiction (pf1-rules#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immediate benefit paired with bodily damage and escalating addiction risk; a world can reduce the benefits or intensify dependence, with continued use and withdrawal carrying the cost.

rules.statement: A drug can be made with Craft (alchemy) at a DC equal to its addiction DC; rolling a natural 1 exposes the maker to it. Ability damage from a dose heals at 1 point per day, so damage also determines how long the dose remains active; further doses can renew expiring effects but add damage and addiction risk.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Drugs — Drugs (pf1-rules#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to crafting risk and a dose duration tied to healing the damage; a world can make manufacture safer or doses longer-lasting, shifting the cost between exposure, materials, and bodily harm.

rules.statement: The plague template changes ingested diseases to inhaled and injury diseases to contact, and raises the initial save DC by 5. Inhaled plagues expose creatures within 30 feet, with repeat saves at most once per 10 minutes; contact plagues can spread by touching an infected creature or an object it touched in the prior 24 hours.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Diseases — Plague (pf1-rules#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to close-range contagion with repeat exposure limited to once per 10 minutes; a world can widen the radius or increase persistence, at the cost of making containment much harder.

rules.statement: Bladed vines grow one vertical 5-foot square per night and stop when vertical surface runs out; they do not spread horizontally. Fire or cold damage makes them grow one additional vertical 5-foot square, while slashing damage destroys them.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Bladed Vines (pf1-rules#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default growth is one vertical square nightly; a world can turn the rate or damage response, with fire and cold accelerating spread and slashing serving as the counter.

rules.statement: A blazing building burns for 2d4 × 10 minutes. Breathing its air deals 1d6 fire damage each round, and every 5 rounds an escalating Fortitude save (DC 15, +1 per prior check) is required to avoid 1d4 nonlethal damage.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Blazing Building (CR 6) — Heat Damage (pf1-rules#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default fire duration and exposure damage follow the stated values; a world can turn duration or save intervals, reflecting how quickly a structure burns and how hazardous its air is.

rules.statement: In heavy smoke, a creature must make a Fortitude save each round (DC 15, +1 per prior check) or spend that round choking. Choking for 2 consecutive rounds deals 1d6 nonlethal damage, and smoke grants concealment.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Blazing Building (CR 6) — Smoke Inhalation (pf1-rules#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default smoke both obstructs sight and causes escalating exposure checks; a world can turn the smoke’s density or save cadence to set visibility and breathing risk.

rules.statement: A blood rain covers a 2-mile-diameter area, contaminating exposed crops and water and imposing a –4 morale penalty on saves and skill checks during the rain and for 4d12 hours afterward. Its poison calls for a DC 18 Fortitude save each round for 6 rounds, deals 1d3 Constitution damage on a failure, and is cured by 2 consecutive saves.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Bloody Rain (CR 8) (pf1-rules#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default pollution and penalties persist according to the stated duration; a world can turn the affected area or lingering time, with shielded resources and purifying magic providing countermeasures.

rules.statement: A disturbed blue benumb patch releases an invisible gas once per day. Creatures in its radius that fail the listed Fortitude save become staggered and take the patch’s listed Dexterity damage; the stagger lasts until that damage is healed, and the cloud otherwise lingers for 1 hour unless dispersed by a gust of wind or similar effect.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Blue Benumb (CR Varies) (pf1-rules#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default patch size sets the cloud radius, save DC, and damage; a world can turn patch size or gas persistence, while damage to the plant or wind can remove the threat.

rules.statement: A Cacophony Crystal amplifies any sound louder than a whisper made within 30 feet for 1d3 minutes. Creatures within 120 feet are effectively deaf, cannot communicate verbally, and lose blindsight, blindsense, and tremorsense; those moving more than 5 feet in a round risk falling, while silence applied to the crystal suppresses the effects.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Cacophony Crystal (CR 3) (pf1-rules#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default sound trigger and affected radius use the listed limits; a world can turn radius or duration, while silence on the crystal is the explicit counter.

rules.statement: A creature that remains in calcifying mist for more than 3 rounds must make a Fortitude save or become petrified. Moderate wind disperses the mist in 4 rounds, and strong wind disperses it in 1 round.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Calcifying Cloud (CR Varies) (pf1-rules#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default exposure threshold is more than 3 rounds; a world can turn the delay or wind thresholds, balancing the hazard against how readily weather clears it.

rules.statement: A catastrophic site treats attacks requiring attack rolls against targets there as critical threats; damaging attacks that require no roll deal 50% extra damage, and effects that neither use attack rolls nor deal damage impose a –4 penalty on saves. Only miracle or a properly worded wish at the site’s center can destroy it.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Catastrophic Site (CR –) (pf1-rules#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default site-wide effects amplify attacks and weaken saves; a world can turn the affected area or the magnitude of the bonus, with extraordinary magic required to end the effect.

rules.statement: A creature inside a Crystals of Telepathic Disruption radius cannot use telepathy or telepathic links. A creature trying to read thoughts there must make a Will save or take the listed damage and be stunned for 1 round.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Crystals of Telepathic Disruption (CR Varies) (pf1-rules#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default radius determines where telepathy fails and thought-reading is hazardous; a world can turn the radius or save difficulty, making the crystal a localized counter to mental powers.

rules.statement: Glue slime entangles anything it touches: creatures anchored to an immobile object have speed 0, cannot run or charge, and take –2 on attacks and –4 Dexterity. A creature can try to escape as a move action with a Strength or Escape Artist check; a stuck weapon requires a successful Strength check to pry free, and the adhesive dissolves in strong alcohol or universal solvent.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Glue slime (pf1-rules#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to immobilizing contact with a check-based escape; a world can make solvent scarce, because adhesive patches also trap weapons and objects.

rules.statement: A creature that eats at a gluttonous site must save or become chaotic evil and gain the ravenous creature template; a temperate or strictly dieting creature gets +4 on that save. An emotion spell effect on the victim negates the effect, and only a miracle or properly worded wish at the site’s center destroys the site.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Gluttonous Site (pf1-rules#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a save against a site-triggered compulsion and transformation; a world can make resistance more likely through temperance, while removing the site requires exceptional magic.

rules.statement: A ravenous creature must eat the flesh of its own kind at least once every three days or suffer starvation; when starvation nonlethal damage reaches its Constitution score, it dies. If it has fed within the last 24 hours, it has fast healing 10, and eating a freshly killed member of its kind heals all its ability damage and drain.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Ravenous Creature — Ravenous Body; Cannibalistic Healing (pf1-rules#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a recurring feeding requirement that powers healing; a world can lengthen or shorten the interval, with starvation as the cost.

rules.statement: An infestation persists despite successful saving throws until specifically cured; remove disease or a similar effect instantly halts it, but disease immunity does not prevent infestation. Gluttony grubs force hourly Constitution checks after the victim has gone one hour without food, with the DC rising by 1 each check; failure deals 1d6 Constitution damage, which cannot be restored until the victim gets needed food.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Infestations; Gluttony Grubs (pf1-rules#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a persistent parasite effect that ordinary disease immunity cannot stop; a world can require a specific cure, while food deprivation drives escalating harm.

rules.statement: Hatelice bond psychically to a helpless host while it sleeps and cause a failed daily Will save to make the host aggressive toward creatures outside its own type and subtype. The victim uses its abilities to attack those targets and gains rage-spell benefits; disease-curing magic kills the parasites, but an aware host may resist the parasite’s mental interference with a Will save.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Hatelice (pf1-rules#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a parasite that redirects hostility through a daily save; a world can broaden spread or sharpen the hostility, at the cost of exposing the host to allies.

rules.statement: A creature that disturbs ill-earth moss triggers spores affecting creatures in the area; those failing a Fortitude save take 1d6 damage to each of six abilities, rolled separately, and repeat the damage if still in the cloud at turn’s end. Fire or electricity destroys the moss, while acid, cold, or negative energy expands it by 5 feet, up to a 20-foot patch; wind disperses the spores harmlessly.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Ill-Earth Moss (pf1-rules#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a triggered spore field with multiple countermeasures; a world can let certain damage types make the hazard grow, turning attacks into a costly choice.

rules.statement: A creature staying in a lust site for more than 3 rounds must save or become compelled to rush to and passionately touch a creature or object at the site’s center, taking no other actions. If that target is a creature, the victim also obeys its commands as if dominated; a target the victim would not normally desire gives +4 on the save.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Lust Site (pf1-rules#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an escalating, site-bound compulsion after 3 rounds; a world can tune resistance based on the victim’s desires, while the effect costs autonomy.

rules.statement: Within a magebane moss patch’s 60-foot radius, arcane spells below 7th level are automatically countered. Arcane casters within 30 feet also randomly lose one prepared spell or spell slot every 1d4 rounds; any kind of damage can destroy the moss, though spells cast from within its counterspell range may fail to damage it.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Magebane Moss (pf1-rules#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a radius that blocks lower-level arcane magic and drains nearby casters; a world can change the affected spell levels or range, while approaching the moss risks losing spells.

rules.statement: A creature that breathes mist must make a Fortitude save or immediately contract schizophrenia. Moderate wind of at least 11 mph disperses it in 4 rounds; strong wind of at least 21 mph disperses it in 1 round.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Mist Bank (pf1-rules#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Make the mist’s affliction automatic after a failed save; a world can tune wind and save thresholds, with exposure and lingering illness as the cost.

rules.statement: Schizophrenia gives a –4 penalty on Wisdom- and Charisma-based skill checks and prevents taking 10 or 20. In stressful situations, a failed Will save causes confusion for 1d6 rounds.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Schizophrenia (pf1-rules#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply the penalties continuously and check for confusion under stress; a world can vary the trigger or duration, at the cost of impaired judgment.

rules.statement: Mourner’s tree spores put nearby creatures to magical sleep unless they succeed at a Will save (DC 17); slapping, injury, and noise do not wake them. A curse-removing spell is required, and a sleeping creature on the ground nearby is buried.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Mourner’s Tree (pf1-rules#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Treat the spores as a save-based area effect and the burial as a separate hazard; a world can vary the radius or escape method, with helplessness as the cost.

rules.statement: A failed Will save against ambient-thought mushrooms lets them detect a creature’s thoughts and broadcast them audibly in the area; leaving ends the effect, and a successful save grants that creature 24-hour immunity to the patch. If more than three creatures are broadcasting thoughts, creatures in the area must save or be confused until they leave.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Mushrooms of Ambient Thought (pf1-rules#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Broadcast thoughts after a failed save and end the effect on departure; a world can adjust the radius or immunity period, at the cost of exposing private thoughts.

rules.statement: After spending 3 or more rounds within a mysticbane crystal’s resonance, a creature with magic must save or be compelled to use its strongest magical attack against itself each round, without spending an action. A successful save grants 24-hour immunity to that crystal.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Mysticbane Crystal (pf1-rules#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Allow a save against compulsive use of magic after exposure; a world can change the delay or eligible abilities, with the risk of self-inflicted attacks.

rules.statement: A revelation bloom’s 40-foot-radius field suppresses illusions, invisibility, polymorph magic, wild shape, and change shape as though an antimagic field affected them; the suppressed effects remain in force and resume outside the area. Any damage destroys the bloom.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Revelation Bloom (pf1-rules#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Suppress only the listed effects inside a fixed-radius field; a world can widen the field or change what it suppresses, with destruction as a simple counter.

rules.statement: Phane crystals can create up to four duplicates per day when a creature sees its reflection. The duplicate comes from an alternate past, has two negative levels, attacks its original, and vanishes with its possessions when either it or the original is defeated; destroying the crystal also ends all duplicates.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Phane Crystal (pf1-rules#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Create a weakened alternate-past copy on reflection, ending it when either version falls; a world can adjust the daily limit or weakness, with the copy’s hostility as the danger.

rules.statement: A spectral grub damages an infested living creature each day and drains its Charisma; a successful Fortitude save halves the hit point damage and prevents that day’s drain. Disease-curing or negative-energy protection effects have a 50% chance to kill it, while a caster who can turn undead kills it automatically.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Spectral Grubs (pf1-rules#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Make the parasite erode body and will over time, with a daily save; a world can tune the damage or removal odds, while delaying treatment risks worsening harm.

rules.statement: A spore patch releases a cloud after a creature remains within its radius for 3 rounds at night, or immediately when disturbed during the day; a creature in the cloud that fails a Will save contracts dementia. Dementia halves the victim’s normal modifier on Intelligence-based and attentiveness checks, and requires an Intelligence check at DC 15 whenever a task relies on memory.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Dementia, preceding Strobe Crystals (pf1-rules#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed radius and save DC; a world can raise or lower patch potency, with greater danger reflecting more potent spores.

rules.statement: After 3 rounds of exposure to magical light, strobe crystals affect creatures within 120 feet. A failed Will save causes the size-dependent primary condition; each round the victim can spend a full-round action to try another save, and success replaces the primary condition with the secondary condition for 1 round before granting 24-hour immunity to that patch.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Strobe Crystals (pf1-rules#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the wall-size table and a 120-foot radius; a world can alter the delay or radius, with stronger displays affecting a larger area.

rules.statement: A talent-leech attaches unnoticed to a creature with a feat and drains one feat per round, starting with the feat having the most prerequisites. It detaches after draining its size-based maximum; drained feats return only through an effect that repairs ability drain.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Talent-Leech (pf1-rules#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the leech’s size-based maximum; a world can shorten or lengthen its feeding, with longer attachment risking greater loss.

rules.statement: During a teleportation storm, once per minute a roll of 1 on 1d6 causes hurricane-force winds to teleport creatures that fail a DC 21 Will save 1d10 miles in a random cardinal direction. Phased lightning can also teleport a struck target into the nearest solid object unless it succeeds on a DC 21 Fortitude save; a failed save causes 2d6 Constitution damage, then 1 per round, and helplessness until freed.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Teleportation Storm — Warping Winds and Phased Lightning (pf1-rules#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated random checks, distances, and saves; a world can tune the storm’s frequency or reach, with unstable reality causing the displacement.

rules.statement: A void rift draws creatures and objects that fail a Fortitude save toward its center by a distance set by the rift’s radius. Entering its central 5-foot square immediately deals the listed damage and transports the target to a plane without air, gravity, or heat, with no save.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Void Rift (pf1-rules#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the radius table and unavoidable central transfer; a world can vary the pull and damage, with a more severe planar tear imposing greater danger.

rules.statement: A witch-grass area makes each ability check, attack roll, save, and skill check roll twice and use the worse result, without a save. Blooming patches can also spray seeds at approaching creatures; failing the listed Will save gives a permanent bestow-curse effect.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Witch Grass (pf1-rules#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the patch’s listed size and seed-save DC; a world can adjust the affected area, with larger patches imposing broader misfortune.

rules.statement: A tormented site triggers when a living creature there fails a Will save: the victim is staggered for 1 minute and takes a size-based circumstance penalty on attacks, skill checks, and ability checks for 1 hour. Only miracle or a properly worded wish cast at the site’s center can destroy it.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Tormented Site (pf1-rules#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the site-size table and stated durations; a world can raise or lower its penalties, with deeper histories of torment producing stronger effects.

rules.statement: A pharmaceutical normally takes a standard action to consume, or a move action when administered with a medlance; each dose weighs one-tenth of a pound. Baseline suppresses, but does not remove, qualifying active effects, while cardioamp can revive a recently dead creature and cureall grants an extra save against one current disease or poison.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Pharmaceuticals (pf1-rules#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated administration times and dose effects; a world can change availability or delivery speed, with faster administration requiring a medlance.

rules.statement: Poisons enter a target through contact, ingestion, inhalation, or injury. Typical onset and frequency differ by route: contact usually begins after 1 minute and recurs each minute, ingested poison after 10 minutes and then each minute, inhaled poison usually acts immediately, and injury poison usually acts immediately and recurs each round; one inhaled dose generally fills a 10-foot cube.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Poisons – Applying Poison (pf1-rules#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to route-specific exposure, onset, and recurrence; a world can make delivery slower or broader, with the reason or cost being altered toxin behavior.

rules.statement: Applying poison to a weapon or one piece of ammunition takes a standard action and carries a 5% chance of exposing the applier; a natural 1 on an attack with a poisoned weapon also exposes its wielder. The dose remains until a hit or touch delivers it, and then is consumed; the poison-use feature removes the application risk.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Poisons – Applying Poison (pf1-rules#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a single-use coating that can endanger its handler; a world can reduce or remove that risk through training or special abilities, at the cost of access to that expertise.

rules.statement: Further failed exposure to the same poison while it remains active increases its save DC by 2 and extends its duration by half the listed frequency interval per added dose. These increases accumulate, but the victim makes one save per interval at the increased DC; satisfying the poison’s cure condition ends all active doses, and different poisons do not combine.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Poisons – Multiple Doses of Poison (pf1-rules#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cumulative escalation only for the same active toxin; a world can make repeated exposure stack more or less severely, with the cost being changed danger or a different pace of recovery.

rules.statement: A harvested dose normally remains potent for 24 hours, reduced by one hour for each hour its source creature has been dead. Harvesting venom from a corpse takes 10 minutes and a Survival check against DC 15 plus the creature’s CR; success yields one dose plus one per 5 points above the DC, up to its Constitution modifier (minimum 1), while failure loses the venom and failure by 5 or more exposes the harvester to 1d3 doses.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Poisons – Harvesting Poisons (pf1-rules#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to perishable harvested ingredients and a risky extraction check; a world can extend freshness or ease collection, at the cost of extra preservation or safer access to the source.

rules.statement: One dose of antivenom automatically neutralizes the first exposure to the specific poison it counters and grants a +8 alchemical bonus to saves against further exposure to that poison. The bonus falls by 1 each hour and the protection ends after 8 hours.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Poisons – Crafting Antivenom (pf1-rules#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one guaranteed neutralization plus decaying, poison-specific resistance; a world can make the protection broader or longer-lasting, with rarity or preparation cost balancing it.

rules.statement: An infused poison first applies its ordinary poison effects, then triggers its stored spell effect and requires a second save. The creator chooses the spell’s effect when making it; poison resistance does not protect against the spell, spell resistance does not protect against the toxin, and poison immunity blocks the magical effect.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Poisons – Infused Poisons (pf1-rules#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a creator-controlled spell payload delivered after the toxin; a world can let the imbiber influence it or alter which defenses apply, at the cost of weaker creator control or changed counterplay.

rules.statement: Necrotoxins require special rites, undead reagents, and negative energy; making one raises the Craft (alchemy) DC by 5 over the poison’s Fortitude save DC.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Poisons – Necrotoxins (pf1-rules#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a harder craft tied to undead materials and negative energy; a world can remove those requirements, at the cost of losing the distinctive soul-directed character of the toxins.

rules.statement: Season sets regional baseline temperatures and precipitation: cold or temperate regions have intermittent precipitation in spring and fall, common in summer, and rare in winter; tropical regions have common precipitation in spring and fall, intermittent in summer, and rare in winter. On tilted worlds, seasons reverse between hemispheres.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Seasonal Baselines (pf1-rules#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use season and hemisphere as the default weather baseline; a world can make seasonal patterns more or less extreme because regional climate and axial tilt determine local conditions.

rules.statement: After adjusting for season and climate, temperature variations are selected by climate-specific tables and last for the indicated number of days; daytime temperature is relatively stable, then falls 2d6+3 degrees at night. Precipitation frequency sets a daily chance of rain or snow: drought 5% with intensity reduced by two steps, rare 15%, intermittent 30%, common 60%, and constant 95%; frequency and intensity cannot go below drought or light, or above constant or torrential.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Temperature Variations And Precipitation (pf1-rules#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed climate tables and caps as defaults; a setting can alter variability and frequency to suit its weather, with the cost of less predictable travel conditions.

rules.statement: When precipitation occurs, its intensity and whether the temperature is above or below 32°F determine its form and duration; a 1d12 sets its starting hour and a 1d6 sets a.m. or p.m. (1–3 a.m., 4–6 p.m.).
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Precipitation Form (pf1-rules#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the intensity-and-temperature tables to generate precipitation; a world can make weather events more or less predictable, trading planning certainty for surprise.

rules.statement: Weather conditions impose visibility, perception, attack, flame, and movement effects. For example, heavy snow reduces visibility to one-quarter, gives –6 Perception and ranged-attack penalties, and after an hour costs an extra 5 feet of movement per square; at least 1 foot of snow instead costs 10 extra feet.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Precipitation (pf1-rules#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply each precipitation type’s stated penalties and movement costs; a world can soften or intensify these effects to make weather less or more hazardous.

rules.statement: Every 10 minutes in a thunderstorm, lightning strikes an unsheltered creature at random; a DC 18 Reflex save avoids half of 10d8 electricity damage, with a –4 save penalty for metal armor. Thundersnow uses the same damage and save, but lightning strikes once per hour.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Thunderstorm (pf1-rules#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use random unsheltered targets and the listed saves as the default; a world can change strike frequency or damage to tune storm danger.

rules.statement: Wind strength can prevent movement and ranged attacks or knock creatures back. In windstorm-strength wind, normal ranged attacks are impossible, siege attacks take –4, Medium or smaller creatures on the ground must pass a DC 10 Strength check to move forward, and Small or smaller creatures can be blown away unless they pass a DC 15 Strength check.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Wind (pf1-rules#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the wind table’s size thresholds and checks; a world can make winds more or less forceful to determine whether travel and combat remain viable.

rules.statement: A creature without food for 3 days or water for 1 day plus hours equal to its Constitution begins hourly or daily DC 10 Constitution checks, with the DC increasing by 1 each successive check; failure deals 1d6 nonlethal damage. Lack of food or water causes fatigue, and this damage cannot be healed until the needed sustenance is obtained.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Starvation and Thirst (pf1-rules#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated survival windows and escalating checks; a world can make deprivation harsher or gentler, with access to food and water determining recovery.

rules.statement: In possible lost-travel conditions, the leader checks Survival hourly using the highest applicable terrain DC, modified by visibility and navigation tools. Once lost, the party moves randomly each hour until it finds a clear landmark or makes a successful check to set a course; the course DC rises by 2 per hour lost.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Getting Lost (pf1-rules#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use hourly checks and random directions as the default; a world can reduce or increase navigational uncertainty through maps, landmarks, and environmental visibility.

rules.statement: At 5,000–15,000 feet, non-acclimated creatures must attempt a Fortitude save each hour, starting at DC 15 and increasing by 1 for each prior check, or become fatigued; acclimated creatures and creatures that do not breathe are exempt. Fatigue ends after descent to air that is easier to breathe.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Altitude (pf1-rules#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the altitude band and escalating saves as the default; a world can change acclimation time or altitude thresholds to reflect its physiology and terrain.

rules.statement: Above 15,000 feet, every 6 hours a creature makes a DC 15 Fortitude save, with the DC rising by 1 for each earlier check; failure deals 1 damage to every ability score. High-altitude acclimation grants +4 on saves against altitude effects, but does not remove the checks.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): High Peak (pf1-rules#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to recurring exposure checks that worsen over time; a world can change the interval or DC because prolonged thin air progressively harms the body.

rules.statement: An avalanche’s bury zone deals 8d6 damage, halved on a DC 15 Reflex save, and buries those struck; its slide zone deals 3d6, avoided on a successful DC 15 save, and buries those who fail. Buried creatures take 1d6 nonlethal damage each minute; once unconscious, they must pass a DC 15 Constitution check or take 1d6 lethal damage each minute until freed or dead.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Avalanche (pf1-rules#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a moving hazard with a central severe zone and a spreading lesser zone; a world can adjust their size and speed because the debris type and terrain determine the avalanche’s reach.

rules.statement: In cold below 40°F, an unprotected character saves hourly against DC 15, increasing by 1 each previous check, or takes 1d6 nonlethal damage. Below 0°F the check occurs every 10 minutes; below –20°F, the character also takes 1d6 lethal damage per minute without a save. Cold damage cannot recover until the character warms up, and reaching nonlethal damage equal to hit points makes further cold damage lethal.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Cold (pf1-rules#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to exposure checks that escalate as conditions worsen; a world can tune temperature thresholds and timing because protection and access to warmth govern survival.

rules.statement: Darkness that prevents sight causes blindness: opponents have total concealment, attacks against unlocated foes have a 50% miss chance, and the blinded creature cannot run or charge. A free-action Perception check each round can locate foes; beating the target DC by 20 pinpoints a foe’s square, while scent automatically pinpoints unseen creatures within 5 feet.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Darkness (pf1-rules#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to concealment and impaired targeting when a creature cannot see; a world can alter how much other senses compensate because darkness blocks visual information, not necessarily sound or scent.

rules.statement: A fall deals 1d6 damage per 10 feet, up to 20d6; a deliberate jump makes the first die nonlethal. A DC 15 Acrobatics check avoids damage from the first 10 feet and makes damage from the next 10 feet nonlethal. Casting during a fall requires a DC 20 + spell level concentration check, except for falls over 500 feet or immediate-action spells; teleporting does not cancel falling momentum or its damage.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Falling (pf1-rules#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to distance-based falling harm and a concentration barrier for casting while falling; a world can change the spell exception because urgent or sufficiently long falls may allow focused magic.

rules.statement: A creature in quicksand checks Swim each round: DC 10 to stay afloat or DC 15 to move 5 feet. Failing by 5 or more makes it sink; getting back to the surface requires DC 15, increased by 1 for each consecutive round submerged. A rescuer using a pole, branch, or rope makes a DC 15 Strength check while the victim makes DC 10 Strength to hold on; success on both pulls the victim 5 feet toward safety.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Quicksand (pf1-rules#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a hazard that holds and gradually submerges creatures unless they act to stay afloat; a world can change the escape checks because the material’s depth and density affect resistance.

rules.statement: A character without air can hold their breath for 2 rounds per Constitution point, reduced by 1 round when taking a standard or full-round action. Afterward, each round requires a DC 10 Constitution check, increasing by 1 for every previous success; failure leads to unconsciousness, then dying, then suffocation over the next three rounds.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Suffocation (pf1-rules#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a breath reserve followed by increasingly difficult checks and a fixed collapse sequence; a world can change the reserve because body size, exertion, and air supply affect how long breathing can be delayed.

rules.statement: To salvage a potion, a character with Brew Potion spends 1 hour per spell level and succeeds at a Craft (alchemy) or Spellcraft check against DC 15 + 3 times the original spell level. Success changes it into a known spell’s potion at least one level lower; failure by 4 or less wastes the catalyst but preserves the potion, while failure by 5 or more ruins the potion and loses the materials.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Salvaging—Potions (pf1-rules#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting a potion into a weaker known effect at the cost of time and catalyst; a world can adjust the failure bands because magical reagents may be scarce and unstable.

rules.statement: Dismantling a nonmagical item takes 1 hour if it costs 1 gp or less, otherwise 8 hours, and destroys it. A successful Craft check against its creation DC + 5 yields materials worth one-quarter its price; failing by 4 or less leaves materials salvageable in a later attempt, while failing by 5 or more ruins them.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Raw Crafting Materials (pf1-rules#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to recovering one-quarter of the value after a difficult check; a world can turn the recovery rate or time requirement because usable materials are costly to reclaim.

rules.statement: A character with the required item creation feat can destroy a magic item and spend 8 hours salvaging it, or 2 hours if its price is 500 gp or less. A successful Craft or Spellcraft check at DC 10 + caster level yields materials worth two-thirds of creation cost; failure by 4 or less permits another attempt, but failure by 5 or more ruins the materials.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Raw Magic Item Materials (pf1-rules#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring the relevant creation feat and consuming the item; a world can change the recovery yield because magical construction materials are difficult to reclaim intact.

rules.statement: When traveling and foraging at the same time, foraging takes twice as long and travel distance is halved. Across multiple terrain types, use the least favorable forage factor and DC; a character can instead raise the DC by 10 to halve foraging time.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Options for Foraging (pf1-rules#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slower travel and a harder check for faster gathering; a world can adjust the penalty because gathering competes with movement and safety.

rules.statement: In moving water, a character is carried downstream at the current’s speed at the end of each turn unless they swim upstream. In water flowing at least 60 feet per round, a swept character must succeed at a DC 20 Swim check each round to avoid going under; reaching shore requires three consecutive DC 20 checks.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Aquatic Terrain — Flowing Water; Swept Away (pf1-rules#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to currents carrying creatures along and requiring repeated effort to escape; a world can change current speeds because water flow determines the danger.

rules.statement: Underwater, fire-descriptor spells and spell-like effects fail unless the caster succeeds at a caster level check against DC 20 + spell level; success produces steam while otherwise preserving the spell’s effect. A non-water-breathing caster must also pass a concentration check at DC 15 + spell level to cast while submerged.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Aquatic Terrain — Fire; Spellcasting Underwater (pf1-rules#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to fire magic being impeded underwater and requiring extra checks; a world can make those checks easier or harder because water disrupts flame and breathing.

rules.statement: In a region with twice normal gravity, creatures move, jump, lift, and throw projectiles at half their usual capacity or range. At one-third normal gravity, creatures jump and lift three times as much, while movement speed stays the same and projectile ranges triple.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Environmental Rules — Gravity (pf1-rules#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to gravity scaling physical movement and force; a world can set the gravity multiplier because local gravitational conditions reshape what bodies and projectiles can do.

rules.statement: A character in extreme cold below −20°F takes 1d6 lethal damage per minute without a save, and must also make a DC 15 Fortitude save, increasing by 1 for each previous check, or take 1d4 nonlethal damage. Cold nonlethal damage cannot recover until the character leaves the cold and warms up.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Environmental Rules — Cold (pf1-rules#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating exposure checks and damage that persists until conditions improve; a world can alter temperature thresholds because survival depends on climate and protection.

rules.statement: When a character has no air, they can hold their breath for 2 rounds per Constitution point, reduced by 1 round when they take a standard or full-round action. Afterward, failed DC 10 Constitution checks begin suffocation: unconsciousness on the first round, dying on the next, and death on the third.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Environmental Rules — Suffocation (pf1-rules#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a brief breathing reserve followed by a three-round collapse; a world can change the reserve because physiology and available air determine survival time.

rules.statement: In fast-moving water, a character who fails a DC 15 Swim or Strength check takes 1d3 nonlethal damage each round, or 1d6 lethal damage if the current runs over rocks or cascades. Very deep water inflicts 1d6 pressure damage per minute for each 100 feet of depth unless a Fortitude save succeeds; its DC starts at 15 and rises by 1 each minute.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Drowning (preceding terrain pages) (pf1-rules#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating exposure damage; a world can make deep or rough water harsher or safer, reflecting local pressure and current.

rules.statement: A character can hold their breath for twice their Constitution score in rounds, reduced by 1 round when they take a standard or full-round action. Afterward they make a DC 10 Constitution check each round, with the DC rising by 1; failure starts a three-round progression from unconsciousness to dying to death, while an already unconscious submerged character begins checks immediately and drowns one round after the first failure.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Drowning (preceding terrain pages) (pf1-rules#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a short, worsening breath timer; a world can alter the duration or failure progression to represent physiology or the drowning medium.

rules.statement: A creature in quicksand must succeed at a DC 10 Swim check each round to stay in place or DC 15 to move 5 feet; failing by 5 or more makes it sink and risk drowning. A submerged creature can swim up with a DC 15 check that increases by 1 for each consecutive round below the surface.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Bog/Marsh/Swamp Terrain — Quicksand (pf1-rules#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to sinking through repeated failed checks; a world can change the checks or sinking rate to reflect the material’s density.

rules.statement: A flash flood sweeps through at 60 feet per round; creatures within 50 feet make a DC 12 Reflex save or take 2d6 damage, while creatures wading or within 10 feet of the river’s edge are swept away by a bull rush at CMB +20. Those swept away take 2d6 damage per round unless a DC 12 Reflex save negates it, and moving through the torrent requires DC 20 Swim checks.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Forest Terrain — Flash Floods (pf1-rules#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fast-moving hazard that sweeps and injures; a world can vary its speed and force according to rainfall and terrain.

rules.statement: A khamaseen storm cuts visibility to 1d6 × 5 feet and gives a –8 Perception penalty; exposure deals 1d6 nonlethal and 1d3 fire damage per hour. It deposits 1d6 inches of sand per hour and usually lasts 1d4 hours to 1d3 days.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Desert Terrain — Khamaseen Storm (pf1-rules#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an area hazard with hourly exposure costs; a world can extend its duration or increase its severity to reflect elemental conflict.

rules.statement: A mirage imposes a –2 penalty on Survival checks to avoid getting lost. After estimating its distance with a successful DC 15 Survival check and reaching that distance, an observer can attempt a DC 10 Will save to disbelieve it; heat haze instead obscures creatures beyond 30 feet and grants them concealment against ranged attacks.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Desert Terrain — Mirage (pf1-rules#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to natural deceptive appearances that distort navigation; a world can let divination expose them or make the visual distortion stronger.

rules.statement: A ghost leech drains 1 point of Constitution each round while attached, becoming easier to notice as it fills: it takes a cumulative –5 Stealth penalty and allows a new Perception check for each point drained. It detaches after dealing at least 3 points of Constitution damage.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Forest Terrain — Ghost Leech (pf1-rules#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a concealed parasite that causes gradual harm; a world can change its drain rate or detection cues to reflect its biology.

rules.statement: During a forest fire, breathing the air deals 1d6 fire damage per round without a save. Every 5 rounds, a Fortitude save starting at DC 15 and increasing by 1 on each check can prevent 1d4 nonlethal damage; heavy clothing or armor imposes –4 on that save.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Forest Terrain — Forest Fire (pf1-rules#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating danger within the fire; a world can modify exposure damage or save frequency according to fire intensity and protection.

rules.statement: A dust devil uses the same rules as a duststorm, sandstorm, or tornado.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Terrestrial Hazards (pf1-rules#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an existing storm or tornado model; a world can vary its intensity because the passage gives no separate mechanics.

rules.statement: A grass fire can be noticed from twice the usual distance of a forest fire. A character caught in its area makes a save against heat damage once every 10 rounds.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Grass Fire (pf1-rules#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the forest-fire rules with doubled spotting range and heat saves every 10 rounds; a world can adjust danger to reflect how quickly wind-driven fire spreads.

rules.statement: A character can locate an aquifer with a successful DC 20 Knowledge (geography) check. A well or pump is still needed to bring its water to the surface.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Aquifers (pf1-rules#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to DC 20 to find a hidden aquifer, then require a well or pump; a world can change the difficulty based on local knowledge and the cost of reaching the water.

rules.statement: Grain can be stored for very long periods, with a nearly indefinite shelf life; dried fruit, vegetables, and meat keep for limited periods instead.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Grains of Truth (pf1-rules#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to grain as exceptionally durable food stores; a world can set exact spoilage periods based on storage conditions and the cost of preservation.

rules.statement: A grassfire’s leading edge travels 2d6×20 feet per round in light to moderate wind, 2d6×30 in strong to severe wind, or 2d6×40 when wind exceeds 51 mph. Each burning area lasts 2d4 minutes, or 1d4 minutes in steppe terrain, and creatures engulfed by the fire gain +4 on Reflex saves to avoid catching fire.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Grassfire (CR 4) (pf1-rules#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use these speeds, duration, and save bonus by default; adjust the dial for wind and terrain because grass burns quickly and is exhausted as fuel.

rules.statement: An instantaneous flame does not ignite green plants, while dried brown plants have a 50% chance to ignite; a flame lasting at least 1 round always ignites desiccated plants. Each round a green plant is exposed to open flame adds a cumulative 10% chance of ignition; wind determines a resulting fire’s direction unless another effect redirects it.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Grassfire (CR 4) (pf1-rules#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated plant-specific chances and wind direction; a world can make ignition more or less likely to reflect moisture and the danger of dry-season fires.

rules.statement: A black blizzard reduces vision to 1d4×5 feet, creates dim light, smothers unprotected flames, and has a 50% chance to choke protected flames. It deals 1d6 nonlethal damage per hour to exposed creatures, can cause choking, has a 10% chance to deal 1d6 electricity damage to those suffering exposure damage, and typically lasts 2d10 hours.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Black Blizzard (CR 4) (pf1-rules#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply the listed visibility, exposure, and duration effects; a world can vary shelter and protection because windblown dust penetrates most seals.

rules.statement: Black lava moves 120 feet per round; a creature in its path avoids engulfment with a DC 25 Reflex save. Contact deals 1d6 damage per round and engulfment 10d6, with half that rate continuing for 1d3 rounds after exposure ends. Ordinary volcanic lava in the passage moves 60 feet per round, uses DC 20 to avoid engulfment, and deals 2d6 per round on contact or 20d6 engulfed, with half damage continuing for 1d3 rounds.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Volcano (pf1-rules#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the two lava profiles and lingering damage as given; a world can vary lava type because composition and temperature change its value and danger.

rules.statement: Earthquakes deal 20d10 damage to affected structures; a GM may increase this by up to 50% near the epicenter and decrease it by up to 50% in outlying areas. A person outside the fault line is generally knocked down and disoriented rather than seriously endangered.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Earthquakes (pf1-rules#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Apply structural damage and location-based adjustment; a world can tune the adjustment to reflect distance from the fault and construction strength.

rules.statement: A typical sinkhole is 4d6 feet across and 2d4×10 feet deep. A creature that fails to notice it moves 1d6 feet beyond its edge before the ground collapses; avoiding the fall requires a Reflex save at DC 15 plus 1 per foot beyond the edge, and falling deals 1d6 damage per 10 feet.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Sinkhole (CR varies) (pf1-rules#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated dimensions and detection and fall procedures; increase encounter likelihood near mines or burrowing creatures because their activity undermines the ground.

rules.statement: At 5,000–15,000 feet, a non-acclimated creature makes a Fortitude save each hour, starting at DC 15 and increasing by 1 per previous check, or becomes fatigued until descending. Above 15,000 feet, each 6-hour period also requires a Fortitude save on the same progression or causes 1 point of damage to every ability score; acclimated creatures gain +4 on these saves.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Fatigue (pf1-rules#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use altitude bands, save cadence, and acclimation as stated; a world can adjust thresholds because thin air and prolonged exposure impose escalating costs.

rules.statement: In no gravity, a creature with a surface to push from can move up to half speed in any direction; a DC 20 Climb check while adjacent to handholds permits full climb or land speed. Once moving, it continues in the same direction and speed each round until it stops, pushes off elsewhere, or creates thrust; nonmagical flyers lose flight for 2d6 rounds on entry.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Gravity (pf1-rules#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed movement and inertia rules; a world can change how readily characters can stop or maneuver based on available surfaces and thrust.

rules.statement: In a dense large city or metropolis, foot travel averages 1 mile per hour; in an open town, an adult’s walking speed is about 3½ miles per hour. Poorly maintained roads and heavily rutted dirt streets count as light rubble and increase Acrobatics check DCs by 2.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Streets and Traffic; City Streets (pf1-rules#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the stated travel rates and rubble penalty by default; a world can change them to reflect its street design and upkeep.

rules.statement: When a crowd sees an obvious danger, it moves away 30 feet per round at initiative count 0. Moving into a crowd-filled square costs 2 squares of movement, and the crowd provides cover that permits Stealth checks and grants bonuses to AC and Reflex saves.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): City Streets — Crowds (pf1-rules#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Treat crowds as moving terrain that grants cover; a world can make crowds denser or more orderly, changing movement and protection.

rules.statement: A character can direct a crowd that can see or hear them with a DC 15 Diplomacy check or DC 20 Intimidate check. Diplomacy takes a full-round action and Intimidate a free action; conflicting attempts are resolved with opposed checks, and the crowd ignores all attempts that fail to beat the listed DCs.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): City Streets — Directing Crowds (pf1-rules#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use the listed checks and action costs; a world can make crowds more or less susceptible to persuasion or fear.

rules.statement: Planes may be separate, coterminous at particular connecting points, or coexistent and overlapping throughout; coexistent planes can be reached from anywhere on the plane they overlap, and interaction across the overlap may be possible. Travel between separate planes requires passage through a third plane.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): How Planes Interact; Coterminous Planes; Coexistent Planes (pf1-rules#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Require a transit plane for separated realities by default; a world can add or remove crossing points, making travel more or less accessible.

rules.statement: Heavy gravity gives –2 circumstance penalties to Acrobatics, Climb, Ride, Swim, and attack rolls, doubles item weight, and halves weapon range; falls deal 1d10 damage per 10 feet, up to 20d10. Light gravity gives +2 circumstance bonuses to attack rolls, Acrobatics, and Ride, halves item weight, doubles weapon range, and makes falls deal 1d4 per 10 feet, up to 20d4.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Planar Traits — Gravity (pf1-rules#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use normal gravity unless a plane says otherwise; a world can intensify or weaken gravity, changing mobility, combat, carrying, and fall danger.

rules.statement: With subjective directional gravity, each individual chooses a direction to fall; a suspended character travels 150 feet in the first round and 300 feet in each later round, in a straight line. Setting a new direction as a free action requires a DC 16 Wisdom check once per round; consecutive failures grant +6 on later checks until success.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Planar Traits — Subjective Directional Gravity (pf1-rules#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Let each creature steer its own fall by default; a world can make control harder or easier, affecting travel and maneuvering.

rules.statement: Erratic time can change the ratio of time passed between a plane and the Material Plane; its example table ranges from 1 round on one plane per Material Plane day to 1 day on one plane per Material Plane round. With flowing time, the plane’s rate is consistently faster or slower, while travelers experience their time normally.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Planar Traits — Time (pf1-rules#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Use normal time unless specified; a world can set a different ratio, making journeys consume more or less time elsewhere.

rules.statement: On a plane timeless with respect to magic, spells with noninstantaneous durations remain permanent until dispelled. Other timeless effects vary by plane; hunger, thirst, aging, poison, and healing may resume retroactively when a traveler leaves for a normally flowing plane.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Planar Traits — Time — Timeless (pf1-rules#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Treat timelessness as preserving ongoing magic by default; a world can decide which bodily processes pause, with delayed needs or harm as the cost of leaving.

rules.statement: On a static plane, visitors cannot affect its residents or their possessions, and spells that would affect them fail unless the trait is suppressed or removed. Spells already active on entry remain; moving an unattended object requires a DC 16 Strength check, and especially heavy objects may not move at all.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Structural Traits — Static (pf1-rules#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to blocking interactions with residents and their possessions; a world can relax the trait or let characters suppress it, at the cost of making the plane less absolute.

rules.statement: A minor negative-dominant plane deals living creatures 1d6 negative-energy damage each round; a creature reduced to 0 hit points or fewer crumbles to ash. Undead instead gain fast healing 2. On a major plane, living creatures save at DC 25 each round or gain a negative level, and creatures whose negative levels equal their levels or Hit Dice die and become wraiths; undead gain fast healing 5. Death ward protects against either strength while it lasts.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Essence Traits — Negative-Dominant (pf1-rules#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to recurring damage or escalating negative levels, with undead benefiting; a world can turn the trait from minor to major, making protection or escape urgent.

rules.statement: On a minor positive-dominant plane, living creatures gain fast healing 2, while undead take 1d6 positive-energy damage each round and crumble at 0 hit points. On a major plane, living creatures gain fast healing 5 and, when already at full hit points, gain 5 temporary hit points each round that last until 1d20 rounds after leaving; while those temporary hit points exceed their normal maximum, they save at DC 20 each round or explode and die. Undead take 3d6 damage each round and are staggered during each round they take it; creatures save at DC 15 or are blinded for 10 rounds.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Essence Traits — Positive-Dominant (pf1-rules#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to healing and accumulating temporary vitality, while undead suffer; a world can raise the trait to major, where excess vitality risks death.

rules.statement: An enhanced spell or spell-like ability functions at caster level 2 higher. To use an impeded one, its caster must succeed at a concentration check of DC 20 plus spell level or lose the spell without effect; limited magic simply fails if it does not meet the plane’s qualifications.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Magic Traits — Enhanced, Impeded, and Limited Magic (pf1-rules#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to applying the plane’s listed magic modifiers; a world can choose which effects are enhanced, impeded, or barred, making its nature a tactical constraint.

rules.statement: Wild magic requires a caster-level check against DC 15 plus the spell’s level or the effect goes awry, with the result determined by a d% roll. Outcomes include rebound, misdirection, replacement effects, failure with or without expending the spell, and—in the 99–100 result—a functioning spell with a –2 penalty to saves and maximum effect.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Magic Traits — Wild Magic; Table: Wild Magic Effects (pf1-rules#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a check and a random table for unreliable casting; a world can remove or intensify the risk, trading predictability for potentially powerful outcomes.

rules.statement: The River Styx can erase memory: a splash causes fugue and full immersion causes total amnesia, each resisted with a DC 25 Will save; native creatures are immune. A thanadaemon charges 50 platinum pieces or two 300-gp gems for a living passenger, but only 2 copper pieces per dead or undead passenger; refusal or violence aboard causes it to overturn the vessel. Paid passage reaches any Styx-touched Outer Plane location in 2d6 hours.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Abaddon — Traveling the Styx (pf1-rules#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to memory loss on contact and paid, guided travel; a world can alter the fare or immunity, with refusal risking immersion and amnesia.

rules.statement: On the Akashic Record, an observer can witness a chosen past event as an immersive scene, but its reflected participants cannot perceive or be affected by the observer. The observer can control the pace, understand all communications, and, for an event from their own life, choose to re-experience it from within; meddling may strand travelers in the past or provoke retaliation.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Akashic Record — description and traits (pf1-rules#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing observation but not intervention; a world can permit interference, at the cost of temporal dislocation or powerful reprisal.

rules.statement: On a finite plane, crossing an edge can deposit a traveler at the opposite edge; borders may be magical edges or the wraparound of a sphere, cube, or torus. Abaddon also has this wraparound trait, while its Styx can provide a reliable route across the plane.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Planar Traits — Self-Contained, Finite Planes; Abaddon — Traits (pf1-rules#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to wrapping edge-crossers to the far side; a world can make its borders impassable or remove the wraparound, changing the cost and certainty of exploration.

rules.statement: An astral projection creates a separate astral body connected to the unconscious physical body by a resilient silver cord. If the astral body is killed, the cord returns the soul to its body but imposes 2 permanent negative levels; if the cord is broken, the creature dies and its soul is swept toward Purgatory.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Astral Plane (pf1-rules#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a tethered projection that returns its soul after projected-body death at the cost of 2 permanent negative levels; a world can make the cord breakable, with death and loss of control of the soul as the consequence.

rules.statement: Astral travelers choose their own direction of gravity and move in a straight line: 150 feet in the first round and 300 feet each following round. Once per round, a free-action DC 16 Wisdom check lets a traveler change direction or stop; after successive failures, later checks gain a cumulative +6 bonus until one succeeds.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Astral Plane — Traits (pf1-rules#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to subjective gravity with fixed straight-line movement and a once-per-round DC 16 check; a world can alter the distances or check, reflecting how disorienting travel through the plane is.
