rules.statement: In the Astral Plane, age, hunger, thirst, afflictions, and natural healing pause and resume when a traveler leaves. Spells and spell-like abilities there can be treated as quickened without changing their spell level, but magic-item spells and already quickened abilities gain no benefit, and only one quickened spell or ability may be used per round.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Astral Plane — Traits (pf1-rules#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to pausing bodily needs and afflictions and granting eligible magic quickened use; a world can change which processes pause or which magic qualifies, balancing timeless safety against unusual spell tempo.

rules.statement: A silver squall usually fills a 300-foot-diameter sphere for 2d6 rounds. Each exposed creature saves at DC 20 each round against the squall’s debate-dependent effect—2d6 Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma damage, confusion for 1d10 rounds, or permanent blindness, deafness, or muteness—and cannot be affected twice by the same squall; a full-round DC 30 Knowledge (planes) check can disperse it.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Astral Plane — Silver Squalls (pf1-rules#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a short-lived, 300-foot field with a repeated DC 20 save and a DC 30 way to end it; a world can choose the debate’s harm, with the storm’s ideas determining the particular cost.

rules.statement: A lucid dreamer makes a DC 15 Charisma check to avoid arriving at a disadvantage. During a dream, the dreamer can attempt impossible feats a number of times equal to the Charisma bonus, minimum 1; each takes a standard action and requires a Charisma check against DC 10 plus the spell level or half the conjured item’s caster level.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Dimension of Dreams — Traits (pf1-rules#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limited dream-reality alteration with a check and a Charisma-based daily-in-dream limit; a world can broaden possible feats, while failure or poor dream control risks an adverse arrival.

rules.statement: Dream-spell effects and conjured items used by a lucid body are not expended in waking life, and dream wounds and conditions do not affect the waking body. If a lucid body dies, its dreamer wakes; a physical visitor instead spends abilities normally, can use dream-generated items only until leaving or the dream ends, and can truly die there.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Dimension of Dreams (pf1-rules#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to safe, non-depleting lucid-body adventures but real danger for physical entrants; a world can make dream visitation more consequential, with physical death as the price of crossing in bodily form.

rules.statement: A dreamscape ends when its primary dreamer wakes; other physical visitors are moved to a neighboring dreamscape or the bordering Ethereal Plane. A physical visitor’s wounds and experiences remain after leaving, unlike those of a lucid body.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Dimension of Dreams (pf1-rules#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the primary dreamer’s waking as the dreamscape’s endpoint and eject remaining physical visitors; a world can preserve or destabilize dreamscapes, determining where stranded visitors go.

rules.statement: A traveler who reaches a moment in their own past can observe safely, but attempting to change that history means they never return: they are erased from the timeline or trapped in a temporal loop. Reaching the moment requires a DC 30 Perception check to stabilize the doorway, and failure ejects the traveler to their starting point with possible severe side effects.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Dimension of Time (pf1-rules#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing observation of one’s past but forbidding successful alteration; a world can change the failure consequence, while the cost is ejection and potentially devastating ritual fallout.

rules.statement: On the Plane of Earth, earth-related spells and abilities are enhanced, while air-related ones are impeded. Native qualities include immunity to earth and acid effects, a 20-foot burrow speed, and earth glide.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Elemental Plane of Earth — Traits and Qualities (pf1-rules#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to enhancing earth effects and impeding air effects, with the listed native defenses and movement; a world can change which elements receive these benefits to express its planar nature.

rules.statement: Earth infusion grants a +2 bonus on Climb checks and saves against earth and acid effects; its improved tier grants acid pit once per day, and its greater tier grants statue once per day.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Elemental Plane of Earth — Infusions (pf1-rules#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these bonuses and once-daily abilities; a world can tune their strength or frequency, with greater access representing a stronger planar blessing.

rules.statement: On the Plane of Fire, fire-related spells and abilities are enhanced and water-related ones impeded. Native qualities include immunity to fire and an extra 1d4 fire damage on a slam attack.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Elemental Plane of Fire — Traits and Qualities (pf1-rules#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to favoring fire and hindering water, with immunity and added slam damage for natives; a world can alter these effects to reflect a different elemental balance.

rules.statement: Fire infusion grants a +2 bonus on Acrobatics checks and saves against fire effects; improved and greater tiers grant wall of fire and delayed blast fireball, respectively, each once per day.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Elemental Plane of Fire — Infusions (pf1-rules#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed skill and save bonuses and daily spell-like uses; a world can adjust availability or frequency to set the strength of its planar blessing.

rules.statement: On the Plane of Water, water-related spells and abilities are enhanced and fire-related ones impeded. A visitor unable to breathe water or reach air risks drowning; creatures made of fire take 1d10 damage each round there.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Elemental Plane of Water — Traits (pf1-rules#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated elemental magic modifiers and hazards; a world can soften or intensify them to determine how hostile the environment is to outsiders.

rules.statement: Water infusion grants a +2 bonus on Swim checks and saves against water and cold effects; improved and greater tiers grant control water and vortex, respectively, each once per day.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Elemental Plane of Water — Infusions (pf1-rules#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed bonuses and daily spell-like uses; a world can change their frequency or potency to represent a weaker or stronger planar gift.

rules.statement: Elysium’s daylight and nighttime lengths are each determined by a separate 1d12 roll at the corresponding dawn or dusk. Its improved infusion grants confusion once per day, with lawful or evil targets taking –1 on saves and lawful evil targets taking –2.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Elysium — Day-night cycle; Infusions (pf1-rules#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to variable day and night lengths and the stated save penalties; a world can stabilize the cycle or vary the penalties to change the plane’s unpredictability.

rules.statement: Elysium’s greater infusion lets its bearer retry a save at the start of each turn against ongoing fear, possession, or mental control, ending the effect on success. The bearer can do this a number of times each day equal to 3 + Charisma modifier, minimum 4.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Elysium — Infusions, Greater (pf1-rules#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to repeated turn-start saves with the stated daily limit; a world can change the eligible effects or number of retries, balancing stronger resistance with fewer uses.

rules.statement: On the Ethereal Plane, spells work normally but their effects stay on their plane. From the Material Plane, force spells and abjurations that affect ethereal beings can reach the Ethereal Plane; other magical attacks cannot cross, and force spells require a way to detect the ethereal target.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Magic on the Ethereal Plane (pf1-rules#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to effects staying on their plane; a world can broaden cross-plane spell effects, at the cost of weakening planar separation.

rules.statement: Ethereal movement uses the action for ordinary movement but proceeds at half base speed, or one-quarter speed without an Intelligence score; swim or burrow speeds can set that rate instead. Flight and non-terrestrial movement proceed at full speed, and paralysis does not prevent this mental movement, but effects that block thought components do.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Movement on the Ethereal Plane (pf1-rules#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to half-speed movement by will; a world can make movement faster or require physical motion, trading convenience for a more restrictive environment.

rules.statement: Naturally formed ectoplasm hinders movement as difficult terrain and provides concealment like dense fog. Ethereal mist obscures sight beyond 300 feet; from 300 to 900 feet, targets are blurry and have concealment, and beyond 900 feet vision is completely obscured.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Ectoplasm; Vision in the Ethereal Plane (pf1-rules#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to these fixed visibility and movement limits; a world can make mist more or less obstructive, changing the value of long-range combat and concealment.

rules.statement: In the Fey World, a native slain there returns after a variable period, often between 1 day and 1 year, or is reconstituted as another of its kind. A native slain on the Material Plane instead dies permanently and its soul follows that plane’s rules.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Denizens; Features and Inhabitants (pf1-rules#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to delayed or altered rebirth for natives at home; a world can shorten, lengthen, or remove the return, with permanent death as the cost of being away.

rules.statement: A non-native spellcaster in most of the Fey World checks caster level against DC 20 + spell level; druids, hunters, rangers, and Eldest worshipers get +5. On failure, a random result may change damage, area, duration, targets, or who is affected, apply eligible metamagic without raising spell level, or summon an uncontrolled creature; the caster may choose to fail the check.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Magic in the Fey World (pf1-rules#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a caster-level check and randomized spell alteration; a world can make magic reliable or more volatile, with unpredictability as the price of casting.

rules.statement: Shaping requires 1 minute of concentration by a character who is not fatigued or exhausted and provokes attacks of opportunity. The Charisma check has DC 20 + 4 per shaping attempt in the last 24 hours; failure prevents further shaping for 24 hours, failure by 10 or more also causes fatigue, and success grants a spell-like effect based on Hit Dice, which must begin immediately in the next round.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Shaping (pf1-rules#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to delayed, tiring, increasingly difficult reality alteration; a world can reduce the time or difficulty, but risks making large-scale shaping too easy.

rules.statement: In Heaven, non-good creatures take a –2 circumstance penalty on Intelligence-, Wisdom-, and Charisma-based checks, and non-lawful creatures take a separate –2 penalty; the penalties stack. Lawful-good spells and spell-like abilities function at caster level +2, while casting chaotic or evil ones requires a concentration check at DC 20 + spell level or the spell is lost without effect.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Heaven Traits (pf1-rules#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to alignment-sensitive bonuses and penalties; a world can soften or intensify them, making the plane’s moral order more or less hostile to outsiders.

rules.statement: Fey World natives slain there can return with their memories and personalities, while their deaths on the Material Plane are final. Heaven’s improved infusion releases a 30-foot-radius burst once per day, dealing evil creatures 1d8 damage per character level to a maximum of 10d8 and blinding them for rounds equal to the user’s Charisma modifier; a successful Will save halves damage and negates blindness.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Features and Inhabitants; Heaven Infusions (pf1-rules#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to native rebirth and a once-daily alignment-targeted burst; a world can alter the return or burst limits, with the latter risking an overly strong daily attack.

rules.statement: In Infernus, fire-descriptor spells and spell-like abilities are maximized and enlarged without using higher-level slots; spells and spell-like abilities that use or create water are impeded.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Infernus — TRAITS (pf1-rules#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to maximizing and enlarging fire magic while impeding water magic; a world could strengthen or remove either effect because the plane’s nature favors fire.

rules.statement: Limbo’s shifting terrain raises Survival DCs to track creatures by 5 in the Borderlands and 10 in the Cerulean Void, in addition to other modifiers. Time is erratic and magic is wild, except on the most stable islands, where magic is normal.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Limbo — TRAITS (pf1-rules#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated tracking penalties and unpredictable conditions; a world could make stable islands more common because they resist the plane’s mutable chaos.

rules.statement: On Limbo’s islands and in its Cerulean Void, gravity is normal. The Void’s pull reaches 200 feet above its surface; an island’s pull reaches the lesser of its radius or 200 feet.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Limbo — Gravity in Limbo (pf1-rules#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to local gravity centered on the island or Void; a world could change the reach because floating terrain and the Void exert different pulls.

rules.statement: On the Negative Energy Plane, negative-energy spells and spell-like abilities are enhanced, and negative-energy class abilities gain +4 to their save DC. Positive-energy spells, including cure spells, are impeded; saves to remove energy-drain negative levels take a –10 penalty.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Negative Energy Plane — TRAITS (pf1-rules#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to stronger negative energy and hindered positive energy; a world could vary the effects by region because some areas are only minor negative-dominant.

rules.statement: On the Negative Energy Plane, exposed living creatures lose their life in minutes or seconds unless protected or attuned; matter breaks down, with food spoiling almost immediately, leather and cloth rotting, metal rusting within days, and stone crumbling to dust. A creature that dies there can spawn a wraith from a metaphysically and emotionally agonizing shred of its soul, while its soul continues to its ordained rest.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Negative Energy Plane — Ecology; DENIZENS (pf1-rules#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rapid decay and life-drain without protection or attunement; a world could slow the process because sheltered regions and safeguards can resist the plane’s entropy.

rules.statement: Carrying at least 1 pound of blight quartz, or being within 5 feet of a deposit weighing at least 10 pounds, imposes 1 negative level for as long as the condition persists. The level cannot cause actual level loss and cannot be removed while exposure continues; it disappears when exposure ends.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Negative Energy Plane — Blight Quartz (pf1-rules#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a proximity-based negative level with no permanent level loss; a world could change the weight or distance thresholds because the effect comes from concentrated negative energy.

rules.statement: A blight quartz weapon or piece of ammunition costs an additional 2,500 gp or 200 gp respectively. A hit forces a DC 15 Fortitude save or inflicts 1 negative level for 1 minute; repeated hits reset the duration but do not stack the level, and it never causes permanent level loss.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Negative Energy Plane — Blight Quartz (pf1-rules#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one temporary negative level per failed save, with repeat hits extending its duration; a world could alter the cost or duration because the energy is powerful but unstable.

rules.statement: When an infused creature reaches 0 or fewer hit points, it can once per day release a 20-foot burst that deals 1d6 negative-energy damage per Hit Die, to a maximum of 20d6. A Reflex save (DC 10 + half Hit Dice + Charisma modifier) halves the damage; the creature regains hit points equal to its Hit Dice, and that healing can prevent death.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Negative Energy Plane — INFUSIONS, Greater (pf1-rules#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to triggering the burst at 0 or fewer hit points once daily; a world could change its radius or damage because the effect spends a crisis to unleash stored unlife.

rules.statement: On Nirvana, spells and spell-like abilities with the good descriptor are enhanced, while those with the evil descriptor are impeded.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Nirvana — Magic (pf1-rules#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to boosting good magic and hindering evil magic; a world could remove or reverse that bias, changing the cost of using magic aligned against its nature.

rules.statement: On the Plane of Gravity, each traveler chooses their own down direction, and unsupported objects stay still. A non-native traveler can move by pushing off a solid surface at a speed of 10 feet plus 5 feet per point of Strength bonus, or use magical movement.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Plane of Gravity — Traits (pf1-rules#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to subjective gravity and require a push-off for ordinary movement; a world could make gravity uniform, at the cost of losing this plane’s unusual movement rules.

rules.statement: Within 1 mile of a portal to a corresponding elemental plane, air-, earth-, or fire-descriptor spells on the Plane of Molten Skies are enlarged without needing a higher-level slot. Within 1 mile of the City of Brass, fire-related spells are enlarged and maximized; spells already enlarged or maximized gain no further benefit.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Plane of Molten Skies — Traits (pf1-rules#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to descriptor-based magic bonuses in the specified mile-wide zones; a world could widen or narrow those zones, with stronger magic concentrated around portals or the City of Brass.

rules.statement: On the Plane of Time, time flows at different rates in different areas and may stop entirely in some. Time-affecting spells, including foresight and time stop, are extended and enlarged without requiring higher-level slots.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Plane of Time — Traits (pf1-rules#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to erratic local time and enhanced time magic; a world could make time uniform, removing both the hazards and the magic benefit.

rules.statement: On the Positive Energy Plane, positive-energy spells and spell-like abilities are enhanced, and positive-energy class abilities such as channel energy gain +4 to their save DC. Negative-energy spells and spell-like abilities are impeded.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Positive Energy Plane — Magic on the Positive Energy Plane (pf1-rules#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to favoring positive energy and hindering negative energy; a world could neutralize or invert this polarity, changing which energy is easier to wield.

rules.statement: Contact with a pre-incarnate soul increases the effect of positive-dominant essence traits on a creature by one step, or doubles major positive-dominant effects, for as long as contact lasts, with a minimum duration of 1 round. Each round of contact also removes 1 negative level.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Positive Energy Plane — Pre-Incarnate Souls (pf1-rules#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to making contact intensify positive-energy effects and remove negative levels; a world could make contact brief or difficult, limiting access to this benefit.

rules.statement: In Purgatory, aging, hunger, thirst, afflictions, and natural healing do not function; they resume when a traveler leaves the plane. Deities with domains there can alter the plane at will.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Purgatory — Traits (pf1-rules#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to suspending these bodily processes throughout Purgatory; a world could exempt some processes or areas, while divine alteration remains the means of changing the realm.

rules.statement: On the Shadow Plane, shadow spells are enhanced: shadow conjuration and shadow evocation imitate effects at 30% power, their greater versions at 70%, and shades at 90%. Light-descriptor spells and spells using or producing light or fire are impeded, and light-source ranges are halved.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Shadow Plane — Traits (pf1-rules#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to stronger shadow magic and weaker light and fire effects; a world could adjust the mimicry percentages or light penalty to change the plane’s magical balance.

rules.statement: On the Shadow Plane, shadow conjuration and shadow evocation effects work at 30% of the strength of their mimicked spells, greater versions at 70%, and shades at 90%, rather than 20%, 60%, and 80%.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Shadow Plane — Magic on the Shadow Plane (pf1-rules#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed enhanced fractions; a world can reduce them toward ordinary strength, since the plane’s mutable shadow material empowers them.

rules.statement: Light-producing sources have half their usual range on the Shadow Plane; light and fire spells are impeded, while effects that produce, use, or manipulate darkness are unaffected.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Shadow Plane — Magic on the Shadow Plane; Vision on the Shadow Plane (pf1-rules#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to halved light ranges and normal darkness; a world can vary this, because the plane remains dim despite added light.

rules.statement: A voidboil produces a burst of negative energy: the usual form covers a 30-foot radius for 6d6 damage, with a DC 16 Reflex save to avoid it; smaller eruptions cover 20 feet and deal 2d6 (DC 12 negates), while potent ones cover 60 feet, deal up to 10d6 (DC 22 halves), and last 1d6 rounds. Tumorlike warning signs allow a successful DC 20 planes check to prepare 1d4 rounds ahead, but eruptions may occur without warning.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Shadow Plane — Voidboils (pf1-rules#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed burst sizes, damage, and warning chance; a world can make eruptions more predictable or severe, reflecting proximity to negative energy.

rules.statement: On Utopia, lawful spells and spell-like abilities are enhanced and chaotic ones are impeded; deities with domains there can alter the plane at will.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Utopia — Traits (pf1-rules#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: alignment tunes magic and divine alteration
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to stronger lawful and weaker chaotic effects; a world can change the alignment bias, because the plane embodies order.

rules.statement: In the Apocalypse Archive, spells aimed at or attempting to affect its structures fail unless the caster succeeds at a DC 30 caster-level check; a successful attempt brings a watcher to investigate shortly afterward.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Apocalypse Archive — Traits (pf1-rules#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the DC 30 barrier and subsequent watcher; a world can lower the barrier, at the cost of making its preserved fragments easier to disturb.

rules.statement: In the Harrowed Lands, planar-transport spells work only after a successful DC 30 caster-level check, and summoning-conjuration spells require a successful DC 20 check.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Harrowed Lands — Traits (pf1-rules#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the two caster-level gates; a world can relax them, because the demiplane resists travel and summoned arrivals.

rules.statement: In the Land of Dread, fear spells gain +2 to save DCs and +2 on caster-level checks to overcome spell resistance. The plane also gradually moves its victims toward places suited to their worst nightmares.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Land of Dread — Traits; description (pf1-rules#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the fear bonuses and gradual relocation; a world can accelerate or soften the migration, since the plane feeds on terror.

rules.statement: A skill challenge proceeds in initiative order through repeating cycles; each participant takes either one cycle action or two half-cycle actions per cycle. The cycle length is set by the challenge’s frequency, and a standard frequency means one round.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Skill Challenges — Running a Skill Challenge; The Skill Challenge Cycle (pf1-rules#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one action or two half-actions per frequency interval; a world can alter the interval, since challenges may span rounds, minutes, hours, days, or longer.

rules.statement: In a movement challenge, a half-cycle action advances up to speed ÷ 10 squares, applying speed modifiers first. A character may spend an action to move backward any number of times, but cannot retreat past the starting point; reaching the listed square total clears the challenge.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Movement-based skill challenges (pf1-rules#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to speed-based progress with a fixed finish; a world can change square scale or finish distance to make travel longer or shorter.

rules.statement: Hustling takes a cycle action and advances speed ÷ 5 squares, but removes the character’s Dexterity bonus to AC unless she has Run. A character can hustle for 1 + Constitution modifier rounds, not necessarily consecutively; afterward, continuing requires a DC 10 Constitution check each round, with the DC increasing by 1 each time. On failure she advances only speed ÷ 10 squares that round and stops hustling for the rest of the challenge; she must rest at least 1 minute (10 rounds) before hustling or running again.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Hustling (pf1-rules#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a short burst followed by escalating endurance checks; a world can change the starting allowance or recovery time to reflect stamina and exertion.

rules.statement: On a successful progress check, a character earns 1d12 + the relevant ability modifier with 10 skill ranks, Skill Focus, or both 5 ranks and the skill as a class skill; 1d8 + the modifier with either 5 ranks or class-skill status; otherwise 1d4 + the modifier. Each 5 points by which the check exceeds its DC adds 1 progress; reaching 3 × challenge CR (minimum 3) clears the challenge. Secondary skills reduce the progress die by one step, down to d3, unless the GM treats the use as thematically appropriate to a primary skill.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Progress (pf1-rules#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rewarding skill expertise with larger progress dice; a world can make secondary approaches less effective or recognize them as primary when context supports them.

rules.statement: A success-based challenge awards 1 success per successful check and clears at 2 + one-third of its CR successes, minimum 2. A natural 20 succeeds automatically; if a second check with the same modifiers also succeeds against the DC, the result counts as 2 successes instead. A natural 1 fails automatically.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Successes (pf1-rules#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a fixed success tally with a confirmed critical doubling; a world can alter the required tally to set task length.

rules.statement: A natural 20 on a progress check succeeds automatically; if a second check using the same modifiers also succeeds against the DC, roll progress twice and add the results, using the original check result for any excess-over-DC bonuses on both rolls. A natural 1 fails automatically.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Progress — Automatic Successes and Failures (pf1-rules#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to confirmed critical successes producing doubled progress; a world can remove or amplify this swing to make expertise more or less reliable.

rules.statement: An ability used in a challenge consumes its normal daily uses and duration, and can benefit a completion check only if it lasts through the entire cycle. A cycle consumes duration equal to the challenge’s frequency; action costs are converted according to that frequency, and effects shorter than a cycle generally have no meaningful impact.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Use an Ability, Class Feature, Feat, or Spell; Frequency (pf1-rules#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to full-cycle duration requirements and ordinary resource use; a world can shorten cycles or relax duration limits, changing how long powers remain useful.

rules.statement: When permitted, Aid Another takes a half-cycle action and requires a DC 10 check with a primary skill; success grants an ally +2 on the next primary-skill check to earn completion or clear an obstacle. Multiple helpers’ bonuses stack, but a character cannot aid and attempt completion or obstacle-clearing with a half-cycle action during the same cycle.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Special Actions — Aid Another (pf1-rules#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to stackable +2 assistance at the cost of the helper’s action; a world can limit stacking or allow broader skills to reflect cooperation norms.

rules.statement: At the challenge’s start, each participant may make a relevant Knowledge discovery check as a free action, DC 15 + challenge CR, choosing to learn about skills or completion beforehand. Success yields one piece of information, plus one more per 5 points over the DC; during the challenge, further discovery takes a half-cycle action. Information may also concern an obstacle the character knows about, revealing its type and then selected details on success.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Special Actions — Discovery (pf1-rules#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to information gained by beating a CR-based DC; a world can make clues harder or easier to uncover, with knowledge and time as the cost.

rules.statement: A backlash is triggered by failing a check to earn completion or gain an advantage by 5 or more, unless its description says otherwise. Its save DC is 10 + challenge CR and its attack bonus is 1½ × CR, minimum +0. With demerits, each such failed check gives the character 1 demerit, which can worsen the challenge’s benefit or failure penalty.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Backlash; Demerits (pf1-rules#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to failure causing backlash or accumulating demerits; a world can increase the harm or cap demerits, trading greater danger for greater stakes.

rules.statement: A movement obstacle triggers when a participant’s accumulated square count reaches its listed count. A count with “+” keeps affecting the participant at the start of each later cycle; a range starts at its lower bound and continues until the count passes its upper bound.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Movement-based skill challenges; Squares (pf1-rules#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to activating an obstacle at its stated position and keeping it active only for marked spans; a setting can widen or shorten those spans to represent persistent terrain or fleeting danger.

rules.statement: Movement challenges usually have 2 + half their CR obstacles, with a minimum of 2. Obstacles are generally spaced at regular intervals, though the GM chooses their exact locations.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Movement-based skill challenges (pf1-rules#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to roughly two obstacles plus one per two CR, with regular spacing; a world can make routes denser or sparser to reflect how hazardous travel is.

rules.statement: An unnoticed obstacle cannot be bypassed, and its attacks treat the unaware character as flat-footed. The first time a character reaches its square count, noticing is checked without spending an action; success permits normal bypass attempts.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Notice (pf1-rules#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a free notice check on first arrival, with failure leaving the character exposed; a setting can adjust how easily threats are detected to reflect visibility and local knowledge.

rules.statement: A character who fails to bypass an attack obstacle is attacked. Its attack bonus is 1½ times the challenge CR, minimum +0, and its damage uses the normal weapon or object damage with a Strength bonus equal to half the CR, minimum +0.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Attack Obstacles (pf1-rules#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to scaling obstacle accuracy and damage from challenge CR; a world can tune those values to make hazards more or less lethal.

rules.statement: A blockade states its material, hardness, hit points, and the number of successful bypass checks needed to pass it. That check count ranges from 1 up to the maximum thresholds allowed for the challenge’s CR.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Blockade Obstacles (pf1-rules#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring repeated successes to overcome a durable barrier; a world can vary material and required checks to represent different constructions.

rules.statement: A failed check at a difficult-terrain obstacle halves movement speed for calculating squares earned. The character is in that terrain only while their accumulated squares fall within the obstacle’s listed count.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Difficult Terrain Obstacles (pf1-rules#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to halving progress while the character is within the marked terrain; a world can change the penalty or span to portray differing ground conditions.

rules.statement: A spell obstacle uses the spell’s save DC of 10 + spell level + half the challenge CR. A magical-device spell attack uses an attack bonus of 1½ times CR; if the effect has no spell level, its save DC is 10 + CR.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Magical Obstacles; Spell Obstacles (pf1-rules#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to deriving magical obstacle potency from spell level and challenge CR; a world can raise or lower the scaling to reflect local magical strength.

rules.statement: A threshold takes effect the first time each character’s accumulated progress or successes reaches its stated count. Thresholds are used only with progress- or success-based challenges and are usually 2 + half CR, minimum 2.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Thresholds (Optional Element) (pf1-rules#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one-time events at listed completion counts and about two plus half CR thresholds; a world can alter their density to make progress more or less eventful.

rules.statement: When the living maze’s backlash applies, a failed check removes 1d4 movement squares. Its dimensional anchor prevents flying characters from earning squares, and its teleporting hazard can send affected characters back to square count 0.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Living Maze CR 8 (pf1-rules#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to lost progress and blocked flight as maze defenses; a world can make spatial restrictions milder or harsher according to the maze’s control.

rules.statement: In the ship-storm challenge, after the second cycle each character must check every cycle to stay on deck; failing while standing makes them prone, and failing again while prone can sweep them overboard unless a Reflex DC 18 save succeeds. Overboard characters take 4d6 damage each round and can climb back aboard with DC 30; a thrown rope grants +5, or +10 if knotted.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Staying The Course CR 9; Thresholds (pf1-rules#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to worsening storm effects by elapsed cycles and allow a rope to aid recovery; a world can adjust the escalation and rescue bonuses to reflect storm severity.

rules.statement: A skill challenge’s CR should equal the party’s APL. For that CR, primary-skill DCs range from easy through difficult, while secondary-skill DCs are one difficulty step above the hardest primary-skill DC.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Determine Base Challenge Rating; Determine Skills and Skill DCs (pf1-rules#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.mechanism: law: challenge rating and skill dcs
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a challenge CR matching the party and the listed DC bands; a world can raise or lower the CR to tune opposition, because challenge difficulty is adjustable.

rules.statement: For CR 1 or lower, a challenge needs at least 2 movement squares, 3 progress, or 2 successes; in general, squares and successes are 2 + half CR, while progress is 3 × CR, with minimums of 2, 2, and 3 respectively. Movement obstacles and thresholds are typically 2 + one-third CR, minimum 2.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Determine Completion; Determine Optional Elements (pf1-rules#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the formulas and minimums; a world can add squares, obstacles, or thresholds to extend the challenge, at the cost of more play time.

rules.statement: A challenge cycle takes 1 round, 1 minute, 10 minutes, 1 hour, or 8 hours. Backlashes generally have an effect comparable to a spell of level 1 + one-third the challenge CR; failure allowances are usually 2 + one-third CR, minimum 3, and demerits usually cap at 3.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Determine Optional Elements (pf1-rules#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed cycle lengths and typical caps; a world can increase failure or demerit limits, trading greater tolerance for a longer or more forgiving challenge.

rules.statement: Challenges can run concurrently or one after another; concurrent challenges are easier to manage when they use the same cycle frequency. Progress- and success-based challenges can usually be embedded in combat, and their rewards may help the party or weaken foes.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Running Skill Challenges Together (pf1-rules#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to chaining challenges or matching concurrent cycle lengths; a world can mix frequencies or add combat, accepting added tracking and pacing complexity.

rules.statement: Chase participants can act for up to 8 hours per day without ill effects, after which those needing sleep must rest for 8 hours. To continue beyond 8 hours, each extra consecutive hour requires a Constitution check at DC 10 + 2 per extra hour; failure deals 1d6 nonlethal damage and causes fatigue, while immunity to nonlethal damage guarantees success.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Running a Chase; Forced March (pf1-rules#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the 8-hour limit and escalating checks; a world can make extended chases harsher or easier, with exhaustion risk as the cost.

rules.statement: In a pursuit, quarry clear the challenge by advancing the required squares; pursuers instead must incapacitate or kill every quarry. In a race, the first group to reach the required square count wins, and other groups lose even if they later reach it.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Types of Chases (pf1-rules#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to pursuit or race victory conditions; a world can alter the objective, changing whether escape, capture, or reaching a destination matters.

rules.statement: Creating a chase disadvantage is a half-cycle action. Its standard DC is 15 + CR for attack or skill checks, or 15 + half CR for ability checks, adjustable by up to 5; success places it at the creator’s current square count, one higher, or one lower. An augmentation can grant +2 to an obstacle statistic, with every 5 points above the DC allowing an extra statistic, target, or +1 bonus, to a maximum +4 to one statistic.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Special Actions: Create a Disadvantage (pf1-rules#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed DCs and +2 obstacle augmentation; a world can tune the adjustment or bonus, with stronger hindrances making a chase more dangerous.

rules.statement: In a pursuit lasting at least 1 minute per cycle, pursuers must track the quarry to earn completion. Tracking takes a half-cycle action, or a swift action with a –5 check penalty; failure prevents the pursuers from earning completion that cycle. Base tracking DCs are 5, 10, 15, or 20 according to ground, modified by distance behind and the quarry group’s size.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Track Quarry (pf1-rules#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to terrain-based tracking DCs and the action cost; a world can require tracking even in shorter pursuits, slowing pursuit when trails are difficult to follow.

rules.statement: Each hour of contesting without resting for at least 8 hours requires a Constitution check at DC 10 + 1 per previous check; failure causes fatigue, or exhaustion if already fatigued.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Running a Contest (pf1-rules#024)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating checks each hour; a world can shorten the safe duration, making prolonged contests physically or mentally costly.

rules.statement: Each turn begins with one full-cycle initial play. Afterward, characters may react in initiative order; each normally gets one reaction per turn, plus one for each point of Dexterity modifier if they have Combat Reflexes. Reactions may trigger further rounds of reactions, until nobody can or chooses to react.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Plays and Reactions (pf1-rules#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one reaction per participant per turn; a world can raise or lower that limit, justified by how quickly its contestants can respond.

rules.statement: A scoring check earns points only if it meets the event’s base DC; where opposed, it must also beat the opposition’s check. In accumulation contests, points build toward a target or are compared at the end; in casualty contests, teams start with points and lose them when scoring events occur, with the last team above zero winning.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Points (pf1-rules#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring both the listed DC and success against an opponent; a world can tune the DC or scoring totals to reflect the contest’s difficulty and length.

rules.statement: A blocker may react to a blockable scoring attempt with an opposed completion check using the skill specified for the contest. A higher result stops the attempt; only one character may block a given check unless the contest allows dogpiling, and the blocker must be in range.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Special Actions — Block (pf1-rules#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one in-range blocker per attempt; a world can allow multiple blockers where coordinated defense is part of the game.

rules.statement: A fake-out names the action the character intends to take and pits the performer’s skill check against each eligible opponent’s Sense Motive. Opponents who fail take a –4 penalty when opposing that stated action; those who meet or exceed the check are unaffected.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Special Actions — Fake Out (pf1-rules#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a –4 penalty for fooled opponents; a world can change the penalty or disallow fake-outs in contests where deception is not plausible.

rules.statement: A character can push herself without spending an action, but only 1 + her Constitution bonus times per turn, to a minimum of once. Each attempt has a Constitution check starting at DC 10 and rising by 1 for each earlier attempt in the challenge; success grants either +1d6 to one scoring check or one extra reaction. Failure causes 1d6 nonlethal damage, plus another 1d6 per 5 points of failure, and requires a save at DC 15 plus total damage taken or causes ability damage based on the scoring ability.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Special Actions — Push Self (pf1-rules#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating effort with physical strain and possible ability damage; a world can change the attempt limit or harm to reflect how dangerous exertion is.

rules.statement: A successful pass sends an object to its designated teammate, who must immediately try to catch it at the same DC; a failed catch does not transfer possession. A pass that fails by 5 or more also costs the passer possession. A successful set instead gives the next allied strike made as a reaction a +2 bonus; a failed set costs possession.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Special Actions — Catch, Pass, Set (pf1-rules#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring a separate catch check and granting a +2 setup bonus; a world can make passing safer or riskier according to the sport’s handling rules.

rules.statement: Effects lose duration by the amount of time represented by each contest cycle. An effect shorter than that interval generally cannot meaningfully affect the contest because it will not last through a full cycle.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Frequency (pf1-rules#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to reducing durations once per cycle; a world can define a shorter or longer cycle to control which temporary effects can matter.

rules.statement: An imbued contest area carries listed spell effects permanently for the contest. A successful dispel or similar effect suppresses an imbued spell for 1d4 cycles.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): SQ — Imbued (pf1-rules#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to persistent area effects that dispelling only suppresses temporarily; a world can vary the suppression time or choose effects to prevent cheating or punish it.

rules.statement: An influence encounter can last up to 8 hours per day without ill effects. Longer attempts risk the target disengaging, which can impose a GM-chosen penalty or cause the challenge to fail.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Running an Influence Challenge (pf1-rules#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an 8-hour daily limit; a world can shorten or extend it, with fatigue or the target’s patience as the reason or cost.

rules.statement: After initiative is rolled, a character can use relevant Knowledge or Sense Motive to identify an NPC; the DC is 13 + the challenge’s CR. Success gives the character and allies a +4 bonus on discovery checks about that NPC, and the bonus does not stack.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Running an Influence Challenge (pf1-rules#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a non-stacking +4 discovery bonus after a successful check; a world can alter the DC or bonus to reflect how difficult the NPC is to read.

rules.statement: A character may try to reduce an opponent’s sway over an NPC instead of gaining her own. The check works like an influence completion check, with a +2, +4, or +6 bonus for the saboteur’s minor, moderate, or major sway, respectively; the effort required matches what the opponent would need to raise sway.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Counter Sway (pf1-rules#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to countering sway at the same progress or success cost as gaining it; a world can make sabotage easier or harder depending on the saboteur’s existing influence.

rules.statement: If disparaging claims about an opponent’s strengths are true, or the NPC believes them, the saboteur gains +2 per such strength on counter-sway checks. A successful Bluff check can make the NPC believe the claims; it takes a half-cycle, with a DC of 15 + the target’s CR, modified for how believable the lie is.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Counter Sway (pf1-rules#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to +2 per accepted disparaging claim after a half-cycle Bluff check; a world can tune the DC or bonus to reflect the truthfulness and credibility of the claims.

rules.statement: A successful discovery check reveals one influence skill, bias, strength, or weakness, starting with the influence skill with the lowest DC; each 5 points by which the check exceeds its DC reveals one more. Attempting discovery takes a half-cycle action, and the character chooses which category of information to seek before rolling.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Discovery (pf1-rules#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to half-cycle investigation that reveals limited target information; a world can make discovery faster or slower, with time and access to the NPC as the cost.

rules.statement: A character can spend a full cycle locating an objective and interact with it in the following round. Alternatively, a half-cycle attempt using Diplomacy, Knowledge (local), or Perception has DC 11 + the challenge CR, reduced to DC 11 if the character knows the objective or has visited it before; failure costs the rest of the cycle locating it anyway.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Locate Objective (pf1-rules#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to spending a cycle to find a goal; a world can lower the time cost for familiar places, while uncertainty risks losing the rest of the cycle.

rules.statement: Whenever a character succeeds at an influence check against an NPC, the opposition takes a cumulative –2 penalty on its influence checks against that NPC. A later successful check also reduces by 2 any penalty the character and allies have accrued from the opposition’s successes.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Opposition (pf1-rules#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a cumulative 2-point swing on successful influence; a world can increase or remove the swing, reflecting how strongly public persuasion changes the audience’s impression.

rules.statement: Each time a character earns the listed sway progress or successes with an NPC, their influence over that NPC rises one level. Minor sway can secure small, low-cost favors; moderate sway can secure resource-consuming or time-consuming help that does not threaten the NPC’s interests; major sway can win risky assistance, advocacy, and concessions in exchange for a suitable alternative.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Sway (pf1-rules#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to four escalating relationship levels, with greater help requiring more trust; a world can make favors more generous or restrictive, at the NPC’s resource and risk cost.

rules.statement: An event takes effect when its specified phase begins, either immediately or after its stated cycle delay, and lasts for its stated duration, commonly one or more cycles or the remainder of the phase. Events can change how difficult NPCs are to influence or impose other complications, and can award or remove sway according to character choices.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Events (Optional Element) (pf1-rules#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to phase-triggered changes with bounded duration; a world can make events more frequent or longer-lasting, increasing urgency and disruption.

rules.statement: If a character uses a favorable NPC bias, influence checks gain +2, or suffer –2 if the bias works against them; unusually strong biases can reach +8 or –8. Incorporating an NPC strength into a roleplayed or circumstance-based influence check imposes –4, while each weakness used grants a cumulative +2.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Biases; Strengths; Weaknesses (pf1-rules#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to modest situational modifiers for personal preferences and tactics; a world can strengthen or soften them, making knowledge of the NPC more or less valuable.

rules.statement: Recognizing an NPC uses a skill DC of 13 + the influence challenge CR; success gives the character and allies the NPC’s background and a +4 bonus on discovery checks about that NPC, and the bonus does not stack. Learning the NPC’s goals can grant up to +8 on influence checks when used to further those goals, while exploiting a hidden agenda can grant up to +12; blackmail may later make the NPC unfriendly or hostile.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Recognize; Goals; Hidden Agendas (Optional) (pf1-rules#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to information giving bounded bonuses, with hidden leverage strongest but potentially damaging the relationship; a world can change the bonus ceilings and the social cost of exposure.

rules.statement: A favor requested by an NPC can count as a listed amount of influence progress or successes when completed; the GM sets the amount partly by task difficulty and margin of success. Favors are run as skill challenges or combats, and their encounter count factors into the influence earned.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Favor (Optional) (pf1-rules#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to converting completed tasks into specified sway; a world can make favors pay more or less, with danger, effort, and time as the cost.

rules.statement: A verbal duel is a success-based skill challenge in which two opponents compete to win successive exchanges with an increasing ante. The duel uses opposition and a distinct action structure and special actions, while otherwise following the standard rules for success-based challenges unless specified otherwise.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Verbal Duels; Running a Verbal Duel (pf1-rules#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to escalating, opposed exchanges resolved through the challenge rules; a world can change the ante or exchange structure, raising the stakes of continued debate.

rules.statement: A verbal duel can run for up to 8 hours per day without ill effects; longer duels can use chase rules, but the GM may penalize the duelist or make her lose outright if others treat the delay as surrender.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Opening paragraph (pf1-rules#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a safe limit of 8 hours per day; a world can allow longer duels at the risk of social penalties or defeat.

rules.statement: At the start, each duelist assigns each skill with ranks to no more than one tactic. Completion checks add the skill’s ranks, +3 if it is a class skill, and the duelist’s Charisma modifier; other skill-wide bonuses grant edges instead, at 1 edge per 3 total bonus points.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Completion; Tactics; Edge (pf1-rules#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one tactic per skill and the stated bonus conversion; a world can relax assignment or conversion limits, making specialists more flexible or powerful.

rules.statement: The duel proceeds in initiative order, using the higher of Dexterity or Intelligence modifiers for initiative. The opening duelist sets the exchange DC with a check and raises the ante to 1; each successful counter raises the ante by 1 and must meet or beat the current DC, then sets a new DC with its result.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Verbal Exchange (pf1-rules#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to alternating checks against a rising ante and changing DC; a world can shorten or lengthen cycles to make the debate faster or more drawn out.

rules.statement: When a duelist fails to counter or ends an exchange, the opponent gains successes equal to the ante and an edge; ending an exchange lets the ender open the next one. Conceding immediately loses, while victory otherwise requires successes equal to the opponent’s Hit Dice plus the rounded-down average of Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma modifiers, minimum 0.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Verbal Exchange; Completion (pf1-rules#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to success accumulation and immediate loss on concession; a world can change the success threshold or concession stakes to make duels more or less forgiving.

rules.statement: An edge can be spent to reroll a completion check, subject to any restriction on that edge. Winning an exchange grants 1 edge, and bonuses from skill-wide effects are totaled and divided by 3 to determine additional edges, restricted to the tactic assigned to that skill.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Edge (pf1-rules#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rerolls as the use of edges and one edge per 3 bonus points; a world can widen edge uses or alter their rate, changing how much preparation matters.

rules.statement: A duelist who wins an exchange takes a cumulative –2 penalty on later completion checks using the skill assigned to the tactic that won it. Countering with the opponent’s previous tactic also imposes a –2 penalty.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Tactics: Last Tactic; Repetition of Tactics (pf1-rules#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to penalizing repeated tactics and immediate repetition; a world can reduce or remove these penalties, allowing more consistent strategies.

rules.statement: A successful audience-seeding check uses Bluff, Diplomacy, or Intimidate against DC 10 + duel CR + audience size modifier: +0 for 2–25 creatures, +2 for 26–100, +3 for 101–300, and +4 for 301 or more. Success grants a tactic-specific edge to a chosen duelist; a failed attempt bars trying that same bias again, and failure by 5 or more bars anyone from seeding that bias for the side for the rest of the duel.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Special Actions: Seed the Audience; Audience (pf1-rules#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to size-scaled DCs and limited, tactic-bound edges; a world can change crowd modifiers or failure restrictions, making audience influence easier or riskier.

rules.statement: In a momentum duel, each duelist starts with momentum equal to Hit Dice plus the rounded-down average of Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma modifiers, minimum 0. Successes instead reduce the opponent’s momentum, and a duelist at 0 cannot continue; the last with momentum remaining wins.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): SQ: Momentum (pf1-rules#028)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to momentum loss instead of success accumulation; a world can use either victory model, making debates about demoralization rather than earned successes.

rules.statement: A character using the background-skills option gains 2 ranks per level in PC classes for background skills; Intelligence does not change this allotment. Ordinary skill ranks can also be spent on background skills.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Background Skills — Gaining Background Skills (pf1-rules#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to 2 restricted ranks per PC-class level; a world can change the allotment to make non-adventuring expertise more or less common, at the cost of character versatility.

rules.statement: Having at least 1 rank in Yog-Sothothery Philosopher imposes a –1 penalty on saves against dread, insanity, and confusion; the penalty worsens by 1 for every 5 ranks, so 10 ranks impose –2 and 15 impose –3.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Profession (Yog-Sothothery Philosopher) (pf1-rules#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a –1 penalty per 5 ranks, counting the first rank; a world can alter the scaling to represent how much mythos scholarship damages the mind.

rules.statement: For a commissioned artwork, the artist pays one-quarter of its listed fee in supplies for each week worked, then makes a check against the quality’s DC. Multiply the check result by the DC for weekly progress in silver pieces; reaching the fee completes the work, and stopping early can earn a lower-quality fee but does not refund expenses.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Background Skills — Artistry (Int), Creating a Commissioned Work (pf1-rules#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to weekly progress and a 25% weekly supply cost; a world can change the expenses or pace to reflect local materials, patrons, and artistic practice.

rules.statement: Lore must cover a narrower subject than the relevant Knowledge skill, and broader topics provide shallower expertise. A partially related Lore check may take a –5 penalty at the GM’s discretion; Lore normally cannot identify monsters unless its subject is a specific kind.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Background Skills — Lore (Int; Trained Only) (pf1-rules#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to narrow, trained specialties; a world can broaden permitted topics, trading precise expertise for wider coverage.

rules.statement: In the consolidated-skills option, an untrained recall-knowledge check cannot answer a question with DC above 10 unless the character can consult an extensive library; using that library takes 1d4 hours.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Consolidated Skills Optional Rules — Recall Knowledge (pf1-rules#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the DC 10 untrained ceiling and a 1d4-hour library search; a world can ease either limit, at the cost of making training and access to references less consequential.

rules.statement: While balancing, a character moves at half speed and is flat-footed; moving at full speed raises the DC by 5. A check is needed once per round, and taking damage requires another check at the same DC.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Consolidated Skills Optional Rules — Acrobatics, Balance (pf1-rules#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to half speed and a repeat check after damage; a world can change these risks to make hazardous movement more or less forgiving.

rules.statement: A deliberate fall allows a DC 15 Acrobatics check to ignore the first 10 feet of falling; damage from the remaining fall can still leave the character prone.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Consolidated Skills Optional Rules — Acrobatics, Soften Falls (pf1-rules#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to negating 10 feet on a successful DC 15 check; a world can adjust the distance or difficulty to suit how reliably trained characters land.

rules.statement: Underwater, a character can hold their breath for rounds equal to twice their Constitution score. Taking a standard or full-round action reduces that remaining time by 1 round; once it runs out, a DC 10 Constitution check is required each round to avoid drowning, and the DC rises by 1 each round.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Consolidated Skills Optional Rules — Athletics, Swim, Holding Your Breath (pf1-rules#029)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to Constitution-based breath duration and a rising drowning DC; a world can change either to make underwater action more or less dangerous.

rules.statement: Hiding a small item on your person uses a Finesse check opposed by observers’ Perception; a dagger grants +2, an unusually tiny object or baggy clothing grants +4 or +2 as applicable, and a frisker gets +4. Concealing it takes a standard action, or a move action at –20; drawing it later is a standard action that does not provoke an attack of opportunity.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Conceal Objects on Your Body (pf1-rules#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to checks opposed by Perception; a world can change concealment bonuses or action costs to reflect how difficult hidden weapons are to carry unnoticed.

rules.statement: When disabling a device, failure by 4 or less permits another attempt; failure by 5 or more triggers a trap, or makes sabotage seem successful even though another device works normally. Taking +5 DC lets you leave no trace, and simple devices can be rigged to fail after typically 1d4 rounds or minutes of use.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Disarm Traps or Devices (pf1-rules#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to secret checks and graduated failure; a world can make sabotage more or less detectable, with delayed failure risking discovery or collateral damage.

rules.statement: A successful Influence check improves an eligible NPC’s attitude by one step, or two if the check beats the DC by at least 5; one check cannot improve it by more than two steps. A shift usually lasts 1d4 hours, and the target must understand you and have Intelligence above 2; you cannot try again on that target for 24 hours.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Change Others’ Attitudes (pf1-rules#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to short-lived, limited attitude changes; a world can lengthen or shorten their duration to make persuasion more or less durable.

rules.statement: A successful demoralization makes a target shaken for 1 round plus 1 additional round per 5 points by which the check exceeds its DC. Repeating the attempt extends the duration but not the severity, and each additional check against that target raises the DC by 5 until an hour passes.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Demoralize (pf1-rules#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to temporary fear that accumulates only in duration; a world can adjust the escalating repeat cost to make repeated intimidation easier or harder.

rules.statement: A successful attempt to pass a secret message lets an intended listener who understands the language understand it automatically; other listeners can decipher it with opposed Perception checks. Missing the check by 5 or more delivers the wrong message, and conveying it takes twice as long as ordinary speech.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Pass Secret Messages (pf1-rules#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to hidden speech with interception and misdelivery risks; a world can change how easily observers detect messages or how costly the extra time is.

rules.statement: Perception can reveal that a creature is influenced by enchantment with a DC 25 check, reduced to 15 if the creature is dominated; the check takes 1 minute.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Sense Enchantments (pf1-rules#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a difficult, deliberate check for detecting enchantment; a world can change the DC or time to reflect how conspicuous magical influence is.

rules.statement: With a Survival check to get along in the wild, you can forage while traveling at up to half overland speed without supplies; for every 2 points above DC 10, you can also feed and water one additional character. A successful severe-weather check grants +2 to Fortitude saves while moving at half speed or +4 while stationary, and can extend that benefit to others.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Survive in the Wild (pf1-rules#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slower travel for sustainable foraging and weather protection; a world can make these benefits harder to obtain when wilderness conditions are harsh.

rules.statement: A trained skill group adds half the character’s level to checks in its skills, and a specialty adds half level when used alone; having both adds the full level. At 1st level, characters receive groups according to class skill-rank progression and one specialty plus half their Intelligence modifier in bonus specialties; they gain another specialty at 2nd level and every two levels after.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Grouped Skills Optional Rules — Skill Group Rules; Calculating Skill Bonuses (pf1-rules#030)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to broad half-level competence and full-level bonuses for matched training and specialty; a world can reduce or expand group breadth to tune generalism versus expertise.

rules.statement: Acrobatics difficulty modifiers from terrain stack across different conditions, but only the harshest modifier within any one condition applies; moving at full speed over a narrow or uneven surface adds 5 to the DC, except for jumps.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Acrobatics — Modifiers (pf1-rules#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cumulative penalties across different hazards, capped within each hazard type; a world can soften or intensify terrain penalties to reflect how dangerous its surfaces are.

rules.statement: A successful check lets a character cross narrow or uneven ground at half speed, making one check per round; while doing so, the character loses their Dexterity bonus to AC, and damage requires an immediate repeat check at the same DC to avoid falling or being knocked prone.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Acrobatics — Cross Narrow Surfaces/Uneven Ground (pf1-rules#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to half-speed cautious movement and a fresh check after harm; a world can make balance more or less forgiving to reflect the stability of its terrain.

rules.statement: A character can use Acrobatics to move through threatened areas at half speed without provoking an attack of opportunity; moving at full speed raises the DC by 10. Moving through an enemy’s space uses a DC 5 higher than the opponent’s combat maneuver defense, and failure costs the move action and provokes an attack of opportunity.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Acrobatics — Move Through Threatened Squares (pf1-rules#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slower, risk-bearing evasion, with full speed requiring a harder check; a world can adjust the risk to reflect how closely its combatants control nearby space.

rules.statement: Jump DC is the distance for a horizontal jump or four times the desired vertical height, and doubles without a running start of at least 10 feet. A DC 15 Acrobatics check when deliberately falling ignores the first 10 feet of the fall, though damage can still leave the character prone.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Acrobatics — Jumping and Falling (pf1-rules#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to distance-based jump difficulty and limited fall mitigation; a world can alter the running-start requirement or safe-fall threshold to suit its physical assumptions.

rules.statement: The optional skill-unlock system grants additional abilities at 5, 10, 15, and 20 ranks in a skill; access can be tied to the Signature Skill feat or a class feature, and making it universal increases skilled characters’ power.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Acrobatics Unchained — About This Section (pf1-rules#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to rank-gated abilities available only through a defined class or feat; a world can make them universal, accepting broader skill-based power.

rules.statement: With 5 ranks in Appraise, a successful DC 20 check reveals whether an item is magical, and a second check at DC 25 plus its caster level reveals its properties. At 15 ranks, an Appraise check at a –10 penalty can replace a Will save to disbelieve a figment or glamer.
locators: Pathfinder 1e skills, environment, afflictions, crafting (d20pfsrd): Appraise Unchained (pf1-rules#031)
rules.speaker: rulebook
